title: US, Israel prepare for fresh Iran strikes after midterms as Tehran threatens with âFather of All Bombsâ
text: Iran threatens to unveil âFather of All Bombsâ amid reports of fresh US-Israeli strike plans The United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed military strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections, according to a report by The New York Times. Meanwhile, Tehran has threatened to unveil a weapon it calls the âFather of All Bombsâ amid escalating tensions in West Asia. The proposed US-Israeli operation could involve a short but intensive campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities and missile and drone arsenal. Watch NETANYAHUS SHOCK MIDTERMS MOVE Israel Detains Trump Rival In West Bank; Big Blow To Mamdani Citing US officials and others briefed on the deliberations, The New York Times reported that the two militaries had stepped up exercises, including flights over Iraq to practise strike manoeuvres. US war secretary Pete Hegseth also met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel this week to discuss the possibility of renewed strikes, according to the report. Some US officials believe another round of attacks could push Iran's economy to the brink and pressure Tehran into making diplomatic concessions after nearly eight months of conflict. However, it remains uncertain whether US President Donald Trump will approve a fresh operation. A White House official said the administration did not comment on military plans âthat may or may not existâ, adding that Trump was keeping all options on the table to ensure Iran could not acquire nuclear weapons. Iran threatens to unveil â Father of All Bombs â Amid reports of possible renewed strikes, Iran has warned that it would respond to any fresh military action. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Iran was preparing to unveil a weapon described as the âFather of All Bombsâ, according to statements carried by Iranian media outlets. âThe United States has the âMother of All Bombs.â We will show them the âFather of All Bombs,â and it will definitely be something new for them,â Mohebbi said, according to Iran's Student News Network (SNN). In separate remarks carried by Iran's Young Journalists Club news agency, Mohebbi said, âWe are in the stage of preparing to unveil the âfather of all bombs.â This is something new for the enemy.â He did not provide details about the weapon or explain its capabilities. Mohebbi also said Iran's missile stockpile had increased 1.5 times following the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025, without providing specific figures. He claimed that missile quality, range, destructive power and accuracy had improved significantly. The IRGC spokesperson said Iran was moving towards a defence doctrine based on permanent deterrence and asymmetric warfare. âNow, we say that if a country attacks us, we will not only respond but also launch an offensive,â he said. âOur doctrine will no longer be merely offensive; it will be asymmetric. We will attack the enemy in a way that makes them feel the intensity of our response,â Mohebbi added. Questions over possible use of âMother of All Bombsâ The Iranian threat follows reports that Trump has considered using the US GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), commonly known as the âMother of All Bombsâ, against Iran's deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility. The conventional bomb weighs approximately 9,800 kg (21,600 pounds) and is among the largest non-nuclear weapons in the US arsenal. Trump authorised its first use during his initial presidential term, when it was deployed against an Islamic State tunnel complex in Afghanistan in April 2017. However, weapons specialists have questioned whether the bomb could destroy Iran's underground nuclear facility, which is believed to be protected by layers of granite. The MOAB explodes above ground rather than functioning as a deep-penetration weapon. Military officials have also raised concerns about its delivery, as the bomb would have to be carried by a relatively slow-flying MC-130 transport aircraft that could be vulnerable to Iranian anti-aircraft fire. A separate report by CNN last week said US military planners had developed strike options that included the potential use of the MOAB against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites. The report also highlighted doubts over whether the weapon could penetrate deeply enough to destroy heavily fortified underground facilities. The bomb could cause extensive destruction at the surface but might not achieve the intended military objectives against deeply buried targets. US builds up military presence as diplomatic efforts continue According to The New York Times, the United States is assembling a substantial military force expected to be fully in place by early November. The planned deployment includes three aircraft carriers, thousands of Marines, fighter jets and Special Operations forces. The report said political considerations, including Trump's earlier pledge not to launch strikes against Iran before the midterm elections, could affect the timing of any operation. The US and Israel reportedly came close to launching another attack earlier this month, but Trump postponed the operation shortly before it was due to begin, despite extensive preparations and heightened alert levels among their air forces. Washington is also seeking to use the threat of renewed military action as leverage in negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme and control of the Strait of Hormuz, the report said. Iranian negotiators, however, have resisted making concessions on the nuclear issue, insisting that it be addressed later in the talks. Some US planners believe a three-day campaign could inflict enough economic damage to change Tehran's position. However, previous US-Israeli strikes between February and April drove up energy prices and inflation worldwide, affected security across West Asia and severely strained the Pentagon's supply of missile interceptors, according to the report. Iranian officials have warned that any renewed conflict could extend beyond commercial shipping and energy infrastructure to data centres and underwater internet cables. Mahdi Mohammadi, a senior adviser to Iran's negotiator General Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, rejected the prospect of a swift end to renewed hostilities. Describing the idea that the US could conclude another round of strikes within 72 hours as a âfantasyâ, Mohammadi said Iran would determine when the war would end. âOur attacks will be more fierce, creative and different,â he said. âWe are determined and confident and strong planning has been put in place.â Pezeshkian says Iran faces a âsuper-challengeâ Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has described the situation as a major challenge for Tehran. Addressing the Iranian Parliament, Pezeshkian said, âThe memorandum of understanding we signed was very good; we hadn't given anything. The current situation is neither good for us, nor for the region, nor for the world.â He added, âWe are in a super-challenge, not a challenge. America didn't think we would stand firm despite the pressure and war, but we stood firm, and we will continue to stand firm.â Iran's representative to the United Nations also alleged, according to SNN, that Starlink had been used to identify and target locations in military attacks against Iran, adding that the country's space and scientific infrastructure had come under attack. The timing of any renewed operation could also be affected by Israel's October 27 election. Analysts believe Netanyahu could face difficulties initiating a war if he loses and becomes a caretaker prime minister. Others believe the prospect of joint US-Israeli strikes could be used to pressure political rivals into joining a unity government. With military preparations continuing and negotiations yet to produce a breakthrough, uncertainty remains over Trump's decision and the scale of Iran's potential response. You use AI every day. title: LDA clears â¹431 cr parking plan, Metro yard and RMLIMS expansion
text: Lucknow Development Authority Lucknow: The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) will build multi-level parking facilities at four city locations at a cost of Rs 431 crore. The projects, aimed at easing traffic congestion and addressing parking shortages, will be built in Vivek Khand and Patrakarpuram in Gomti Nagar, near Ekana Stadium, and at Ambedkar Park. The proposals were approved at the LDA board meeting chaired by divisional commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant on Monday. The four facilities will have a combined capacity of more than 1,500 vehicles, said LDA secretary SP Singh. Vivek Khand and Patrakarpuram face parking shortages due to commercial activity, while Ekana Stadium experiences traffic congestion during matches and major events. Visitors to Ambedkar Park also frequently park their vehicles along roads. The facilities will be developed under the central govtâs urban challenge fund. Land for RMLIMS expansion The board approved allocating land in Sector 7 of Gomti Nagar Extension to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences (RMLIMS) for expansion of its hospital building. Around 1,000 beds are in the plans. Fire station in Priyadarshini Colony The LDA will provide 2,600 square metres of land in Sector C of Priyadarshini Colony free of cost for a fire station. The proposal followed a request from the fire department after the fire incident in Aliganj. War Museum and Convention Centre The board also considered the proposal to develop a War Museum and Convention Centre in Gomti Nagar. The project is among the major infrastructure and public development proposals considered at the meeting. Metro yard in Basant Kunj The board approved allocating 20.358 acres in Basant Kunj for a Metro yard. A fish market and a flower market currently operate on the site. The LDA will arrange to relocate both markets and identify alternative land for them. The land allocation is expected to facilitate Metro construction work. Land for bus terminal Around 7.5 hectares of land in the Basant Kunj scheme will be provided for the construction of a new bus terminal. Upcoming Housing Scheme The LDA board approved layouts for the upcoming phases of Varun Vihar and Naimish Nagar, along with land-use change for Varun Vihar. LDA Vice Chairperson Prathmesh Kumar said the decision taken in the meeting will be implemented soon. The board approved more than 12 development proposals and passed the authorityâs budget for the next financial year. The meeting was attended by additional secretary Gyanendra Verma and other officials from the Municipal Corporation, public works department and district administration. title: SC upholds war injury pension for Army man in Op Rakshak
text: Chandigarh: The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal filed by the Union of India challenging the grant of âwar injury pensionâ to an Army personnel who developed rheumatoid arthritis (seropositive) while posted at Kargil during Operation Rakshak, holding that the ministry of defence could not deny pensionary benefits when its policy did not distinguish between operations notified by the govt. A bench of Justices Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, while upholding the decisions of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) and the Punjab and Haryana high court, also directed that while notifying operations under Category E(i) of the MoD policy, Govt must declare in clear terms whether the pensionary benefits contemplated under the policy would apply to such notifications. Narender Kumar, who was enrolled in the Indian Army on Dec 30, 1996, was posted in Kargil from July 13, 2003, to July 6, 2005, when he was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (seropositive). He was later diagnosed with two other spinal disabilities while posted in West Bengal. The Release Medical Board, while discharging him from service on January 31, 2013, conceded all three disabilities as aggravated by military service at 70% for life, rounded off to 75% for life. Having rendered more than 16 years of service, he was granted disability pension consisting of service element and disability element. Six years after his discharge, he approached the AFT seeking war injury pension under Part II, Category E(i), Para 4.1 of the MoD policy letter dated Jan 31, 2001, contending that the disability was a direct consequence of his posting at Kargil during Operation Rakshak. MoD argued his disability was not covered under Category E(i) of the policy. The AFT, in April 2024, allowed his application, holding that the disease originated in Jan 2005 when he was serving at Kargil and that the entire Jammu and Kashmir area was an operational area. The Punjab and Haryana high court dismissed the ministryâs challenge in Aug 2025. Before the Supreme Court, additional solicitor general Archana Pathak Dave argued the respondentâs claim did not fall under Category E(i). The Centre maintained that Category E(i) would cover only operations specially notified by the govt, such as Operation Sindoor or Operation Snow Leopard, and not ongoing operations such as Operation Rakshak, which covers the entire Jammu and Kashmir, or Operation Rhino, covering the entire Assam. Kumarâs counsel, advocate Ajay Sehoran, submitted that Operation Rakshak at Kargil was an integral part of operations specially notified by the govt under Category E(i). Referring to Army Order 1 of 2003, the counsel argued that battle casualties included casualties occurring while operating on the International Border or Line of Control due to natural calamities and illnesses caused by climatic conditions. Examining the scope of Category E(i), the Supreme Court observed, âSub-Category E(i) is intended to give flexibility to our defence administration as it is natural that all war-like situations cannot comprehensively commence and conclude within the specified eight Sub-Categories (a) to (h).â The bench added: âGoing by the plain language of the policy, once a notification is issued for a specific operation, Category E(i) is invoked, unless there is something indicative either in the Policy or in the notification so issued.â It added, âExcept for the oral statement of the Ld. ASG that Operation Rakshak is not intended to be covered under Category E(i), there is no other interpretative aid for us to exclude Operation Rakshak from the scope of Category E(i).â The Bench observed, âIf the policymaker interprets its own policy against the plain language or in a manner that could be discriminatory, arbitrary, irrational or goes against the very purpose and object of the policy, the courts will disregard the interpretation offered by the policymaker.â The Supreme Court held that Category E(i) was enabling in nature and that when the language of the policy was unrestrictive, it was not for the court to limit its application through an interpretative process, particularly when the policy concerned grant of pensionary benefits. The bench also observed that the MoD policy letter of 2001 was clear and that when there was no distinction between notifications issued under Category E(i), the benefit of the policy could not be denied. The bench, however, added that âwhile notifying operations as contemplated under Category E(i), the Government must declare in clear terms whether the pensionary benefits contemplated under Para 4.1, Category E(i) of the MoD Policy letter dated 31.01.2001 would be applicable to such notification or not.â You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in Chandigarh Stay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. title: Scientists find twin and triplet embryos inside two eggs laid by one wild Burmese python in Florida, marking a first for snakes
text: Image AI generated Scientists have discovered twin and triplet embryos inside two eggs laid by a single wild Burmese python in southern Florida, marking the first recorded instance of triplet embryos in a snake. The unusual finding emerged from a clutch of 37 eggs laid on 17 May 2024 by a radio-tagged female python in Big Cypress National Preserve. While 32 eggs hatched normally, researchers found two non-viable eggs containing five embryos in total, all of which had died before hatching. According to the study published in Ecology and Evolution titled â First Record of Twin and Triplet Embryos Found in the Clutch of a Wild Burmese Python in Southern Florida â, the discovery raises questions about how multiple embryos develop within a single snake egg and how often such occurrences happen in the wild. What did scientists discover inside the Burmese python eggs The unusual clutch was laid on 17 May 2024 by a female Burmese python measuring 313.7 centimetres in snout-to-vent length. The eggs were deposited within a hardwood hammock in Big Cypress National Preserve, where researchers were already monitoring python reproduction and survival as part of a long-term study. The clutch was monitored in its natural location, allowing scientists to observe the development and eventual hatching of the eggs. On 14 July 2024, researchers removed the female from the clutch before the expected hatching period to install an enclosure designed to prevent hatchlings from escaping. The enclosure consisted of a polyvinyl chloride frame covered with two nested mesh laundry bags. Non-viable eggs were removed during the process, while trail cameras were used to monitor the remaining eggs remotely. Hatching began on 17 July, and researchers collected, weighed and measured the emerging hatchlings over five days; the process completed on 22 July 2024. PC: First Record of Twin and Triplet Embryos Found in the Clutch of a Wild Burmese Python in Southern Florida How were the twin embryos inside Egg A different in their development The first unusual egg, identified as Egg A, contained two female embryos. When researchers examined it on 22 July, they found a two-centimetre slit in its shell, indicating that the hatching process, known as pipping, had begun. Both embryos were attached to the same yolk and had died. Their development, however, was not identical. One embryo had developed more extensive pigmentation but showed significant skeletal and developmental abnormalities, while the other had a more normally developed body and intact organs. The second egg, identified as Egg B, contained three embryos at different developmental stages. Unlike Egg A, this egg remained intact, with no signs that hatching had begun. Two of the embryos were similar in size and weight, while the third was considerably smaller and less developed. The researchers recorded that the smallest embryo weighed just 5.6 grams and had a compressed body, particularly around the head and neck. The sexes of all three embryos could not be determined. All were connected to the same yolk, much of which remained unabsorbed. What is monozygotic twinning, and how does it occur in reptiles The study also examined how multiple embryos might develop inside a single reptile egg. Researchers explained that twinning can occur when one fertilised egg divides into two independent embryos, a process known as monozygotic twinning. Another possibility is dizygotic twinning, in which two separately fertilised eggs, each with its own yolk sac, become enclosed within the same eggshell. Scientists have previously proposed that differences in embryo size and egg dimensions could help distinguish between these processes. In the Burmese python clutch, however, both unusual eggs were similar in size to the other eggs, and all embryos were connected to a single yolk. The two embryos in Egg A also had similar body masses, observations that suggested a possible monozygotic origin. However, the researchers cautioned that physical characteristics alone could not establish how the embryos originated. They noted that yolk sacs may fuse to form a common yolk sac, meaning further genetic testing would be necessary to determine the embryos' origins conclusively. Why are twin and triplet embryos so rare in wild Burmese pythons The researchers noted that multiple-embryo eggs are reported in other reptiles, including lizards, turtles and crocodiles, but documented cases in snakes have been considerably more limited. Earlier reports of snake twins had largely involved captive-bred individuals or wild-caught females that laid eggs in captivity. The first documented Burmese python twins came from a captive-bred clutch in which two eggs each contained a pair of embryos. Neither pair survived to hatch. Before the southern Florida discovery, the scientific literature had not documented triplet embryos in snakes. The researchers also highlighted that the frequency of such eggs in wild Burmese pythons remains unknown. Previous observations of wild python clutches in southern Florida had not identified similar cases. The female involved in the study had also laid a clutch in May 2022 of 19 viable eggs and one non-viable egg, none of which contained multiple embryos. The authors described the occurrence as uncommon based on their observations and stressed that further research is needed to establish how frequently it happens, whether such embryos can survive to hatching and how these unusual reproductive events affect the species' overall reproductive output. Although none of the five embryos in the 2024 clutch survived, the discovery provides a documented example of both twin and triplet development in eggs laid by a wild snake.

title: Queenslandâs Kuridala copper town prospered during World War I, but a 1918 cyclone damaged its smelter before the plant closed in 1920
text: Representative Image of the historic Hampden Smelter and railway, highlighting their role in Kuridalaâs mining prosperity (AI-generated image) Kuridala, about 65â70 km south of Cloncurry in Queensland, grew into an important copper-mining settlement before and during World War I. Its development was closely tied to the Hampden Smelter and a railway connection that helped transport ore from the surrounding mining district. But the townâs prosperity depended on the copper industry, leaving it exposed to changing prices, operational disruptions and financial pressures. Queensland Places records Kuridalaâs population at about 1,500 in 1913 before reporting 774 by 1921. The Queensland Heritage Register gives different figures, recording a population of 2,000 by 1920 and 800 by 1924. How the Hampden Smelter and railway helped build Kuridala Kuridala developed through several name changes. The Queensland Heritage Register records that the settlement was surveyed as Hampden in 1910 and known as Friezland by 1912 before officially becoming Kuridala in October 1916. Queensland Places gives an earlier sequence that begins with Gulatten, followed by Friezland and Kuridala. According to the Heritage Register, the final name was intended to avoid confusion with another Queensland settlement, although anti-German sentiment has also been suggested as a possible factor during the war. Railway development and copper processing were central to the townâs growth. The railway reached Cloncurry in 1908, with an extension serving the Hampden area opening in 1910. The Hampden Smelter began operating in March 1911 and continued until 1920, allowing copper ore from nearby mines to be processed locally. The smelter helped support a substantial settlement, with businesses and public services developing around the mining industry. By 1913, Kuridala had about 1,500 residents, according to Queensland Places. The town had hotels, shops, an ice works, a printery, a hospital, churches and a school. These facilities reflected the needs of a community whose employment and commercial activity were closely connected to mining and smelting. World War I sustained the regionâs prosperity rather than initiating Kuridalaâs growth. The Queensland Heritage Register describes the conflict as bringing four years of prosperity to the Cloncurry district and notes that the period was particularly prosperous for the company operating the smelter. Queensland Places identifies 1918 as a high point for the settlement. It records a daily school attendance of 280 children, while the Heritage Register describes the school as having up to 280 pupils. Why Kuridala declined after World War I Kuridalaâs fortunes changed as the conditions supporting copper production weakened. British wartime price controls ended in 1918, and the Queensland Heritage Register says the change forced the company into difficulties. In December 1918, a cyclone damaged the smelter and its powerhouse. Smelting was postponed until September 1919. The plant processed about 69,598 long tons of ore in 1920, equivalent to approximately 70,715 tonnes, according to the Heritage Register. The smelterâs closure was also connected to financial difficulties. The Heritage Register records that the Commonwealth Bank withdrew funds against copper awaiting export, after which the company halted all operations. Queensland Places also identifies the collapse in copper prices in 1920 as a factor in the townâs decline. Population figures from the period differ between the sources. Queensland Places reports 774 residents by 1921, while the Heritage Register records 2,000 by 1920 and 800 by 1924. As mining and smelting activity contracted, facilities that had supported the settlement were moved elsewhere. The hospital, picture theatre and courthouse were relocated to Mount Isa, while the ice works also followed. The Queensland Heritage Register records that the company ceased to exist in 1928, after offering its assets for sale in 1926 and their subsequent purchase by Mount Elliott. Kuridala today: the heritage significance of the Hampden Smelter The remains of the Hampden Smelter are central to Kuridalaâs historical significance. The Queensland Heritage Register identifies the site as evidence of the copper industry that helped shape the Cloncurry district. Its surviving industrial remains also have research potential for understanding the technology, organisation and operation of early 20th-century copper smelting. Kuridalaâs history records the rise of a mining settlement supported by railway access and industrial investment, followed by the contraction of its principal industry. The surviving smelter remains, and historical records document the townâs place in Queenslandâs copper-mining history. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: Germany, South Korea enhance strategic, security ties against backdrop of China-Russia-North Korea collusive threat
text: The summit and the Asia-Pacific Conference comes against the backdrop of Russiaâs full-scale war against Ukraine that has seen more than 10,000 North Korean soldiers participate in that war on Russiaâs behalf. SEOUL: Ahead of the 19th Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business here in the South Korean capital, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz held a summit with South Koreaâs President Lee Jae-myung, setting out a roadmap for an enhanced security partnership and raising their overall bilateral relationship to an Enhanced Strategic Partnership. Both sides agreed to deepen their ties in security and defence through regular military exchanges, training cooperation, and to conclude a bilateral agreement on the protection of classified military information. President Lee also expressed the interest of Korean defence companies in forming long-term partnerships with Germany, including through joint ventures and joint development projects. The summit and the Asia-Pacific Conference comes against the backdrop of Russiaâs full-scale war against Ukraine that has seen more than 10,000 North Korean soldiers participate in that war on Russiaâs behalf. This has raised serious concerns in Seoul that North Korean soldiers have gained high-tech battlefield experience that could now be deployed by Pyongyang on the Korean Peninsula. Meanwhile, Chinaâs domination of global supply chains has allowed Beijing to provide industrial support to Russia and help it evade sanctions, thereby keeping Moscowâs war machinery going. Chancellor Merz, who has been on a week-long tour of East Asia with stopovers in Singapore and Japan, has been critical of this China-Russia collusion. In Singapore, Merz demanded that Beijing use its influence over Moscow to ensure a just peace in Ukraine, and called for strengthening economic relations between Europe and the Indo-Pacific region to reduce one-sided dependence on China. The wars in Ukraine and Iran, and Chinaâs fingerprints on both conflict theatres, have sharply brought home the point that Europeâs economic and security interests are intertwined with that of Asiaâs. And it is this reality that is compelling German businesses, as represented in the Asia-Pacific Conference, to look for resilient supply chains, non-hegemonic partnerships in critical technologies like AI, semiconductors and batteries, and cultivate suitable leverage against Chinaâs weaponisation of its industrial domination. title: Noida clears decks to allot 13,000 more abadi plots in urban villages
text: The 2031 master plan envisages acquisition of 15,279 hectares of land Noida: Noida Authority has amended its Master Plan 2031 to resolve pending cases involving the allotment of 5% developed residential plots to farmers. The amendment provides for earmarking these plots on land adjoining existing village abadi areas and is expected to pave the way for allotment to nearly 13,000 farmers who gave up their land for development projects but are yet to receive developed plots that were part of the compensation package. Noida, Greater Noida and Yamuna authorities currently follow a policy of giving farmers 5%, 6% and 7% of developed plots respectively in return for acquired land. Allotment has been planned in several cases, but farmers claim nearly 12,800 beneficiaries are still awaiting developed plots. âSince the master plan 2031 is nearing full implementation, identifying suitable locations for planning and allotting the remaining plots has become difficult. In view of farmersâ demand for an early resolution of these cases, the Authority has decided to amend the master plan to allow 5% abadi plots on land adjoining existing village abadi,â a Noida Authority official said. Officials said the Authority will now invite objections and suggestions from the public before sending the proposal to the state government for approval. Once the amendment is approved, the Authority will acquire suitable land and allot plots to eligible farmers. Over the past decade, Noida has seen multiple protests by farmers seeking 64.7% additional compensation and 10% developed plots. The most recent was held on Oct 7, when farmers under the banner of BKU (Manch) protested outside the Authorityâs Sector 96 office and demanded developed plots in return for land acquired for planned development. The demand stems from the Allahabad High Courtâs Oct 2011 order in the Gajraj versus State of UP case, which directed payment of an additional 64.7% compensation over and above the amount already paid to farmers, besides allotment of developed residential plots equivalent to 10% of the acquired land. So far, Noida Authority has paid enhanced compensation to farmers, but developed plots have not been allotted to many of the affected farmers because of a shortage of land. The 2031 master plan envisages acquisition of 15,279 hectares of land. According to a 2021 CAG audit, the Authority acquired nearly 12,375 hectares in 69 villages between its formation in 1976 and 2020. In Feb 2024, UP govt constituted a three-member high-powered committee to examine the issue. The panel, comprising revenue board chairperson Rajneesh Dube, then Noida district magistrate Manish Kumar and Meerut divisional commissioner Selva Kumari J, examined the farmersâ demands and submitted its report in Aug 2024, which concluded that, based on documentary evidence and its analysis, the demands were not found to be justified or practical, and that it was not possible to form an opinion on some of the issues raised by farmers. The amendment is likely to accelerate construction and push up land values in Hajipur, Salarpur, Bhangel and Sorkha villages that are located close to developed sectors. However, the scale of growth will depend on the identification availability of land and the allotment process. title: CAG Flags NMCâs Rs1,646cr Pending Utilisation Certificates, Negative Balance In Smart City Account
text: CAG Audit Nagpur: A Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) inspection audit of Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) has flagged several financial and accounting lapses, including pending utilisation certificates (UCs) worth Rs1,646 crore, unadjusted advances of Rs4.2 crore and a negative balance of Rs52.44 crore in the Nagpur Smart and Sustainable City Development Corporation Ltd account (NSSCDCL). The audit observations raise questions about the civic bodyâs financial management, monitoring of govt grants and internal accounting controls. The findings are part of the inspection report on the accounts of NMCâs chief accounts and finance officer for the period covered by the audit. One of the major concerns is the non-submission of utilisation certificates worth Rs1,646 crore. The pending certificates relate to grants received from govt agencies and are required to establish that funds were spent for their sanctioned purposes. The delay could complicate financial accountability and affect the processing of future grants. The audit also highlights a negative balance of Rs52.44 crore in the account of NSSCDCL. The provisional balance sheet for 2024-25 showed the deficit under grants and contributions for specific purposes. The report also recorded a reduction in the grant balance for special city development projects. Another observation concerns advances of Rs4.20 crore paid to various officials and department heads that remain unadjusted. The audit sought details of pending advances, indicating shortcomings in monitoring and reconciliation of expenditure. The report also raised concerns over statutory accounting procedures. While NMCâs annual accounts for 2023-24 were examined and approved by the chief auditor, the accounts for 2024-25 had been prepared but further action was still underway. The audit sought an update on compliance with statutory requirements. Among other outstanding observations are a loan liability of Rs94.41 crore pending for over 16 years and avoidable interest payments linked to delays in loan-related procedures. Former NCP corporator Vedprakash Arya submitted a memorandum to municipal commissioner Vipin Itankar, demanding a high-level inquiry into the financial irregularities and accountability of officials concerned. title: Iran's Supreme leader calls for 'geographically unrestricted' response to enemy threats
text: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has directed the military to prepare for immediate responses to potential threats Iran's Supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the country's armed forces to prepare an immediate and "geographically unrestricted response" to any enemy threat, warning that Tehran will decide the timing and terms of any future conflict if the United States or Israel resumes military or terrorist attacks. According to Reuters, in a written message, Khamenei directed the armed forces to update their target lists to bring "all US and Israeli assets, tangible and intangible," within striking range, while ordering an increase in ammunition and weapons production and stronger military intelligence and indigenous defence capabilities. In his message, Khamenei called for an immediate and forceful response to any threat, making clear that Iran would not limit the geographical scope of its retaliation. "Immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response" to any enemy threat, he said. He further asserted that Tehran would decide the timing and conditions for ending any future confrontation, warning that any renewed military or terrorist attacks would trigger a fresh conflict. Beyond expanding its potential target range, Khamenei also called for strengthening Iran's military production capacity, directing the armed forces to increase the manufacturing of ammunition and weapons for reconnaissance, support and combat operations. He also instructed the military to strengthen its intelligence capabilities and develop indigenous defence systems, according to the written message. The directives indicate Tehran's focus on improving its ability to gather intelligence, sustain military operations and reduce dependence on foreign suppliers for critical defence equipment. The latest directives come as tensions continue to escalate between Tehran and Washington over the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing military confrontation. Iran has repeatedly warned that any fresh US or Israeli attack would trigger retaliation, while diplomatic efforts involving regional countries have so far failed to produce a breakthrough. title: The political obituary can wait: Lula, Bibi and the art of survival
text: Lula won, Netanyahu wouldnât lose: The art of political survival One is a Left-wing icon challenging Trump's dominance of Latin America. The other is a Right-wing nationalist who helped persuade the US president to attack Iran. Yet, despite their ideological differences, Lula and Netanyahu have shown why writing political obituaries can be a dangerous business. Opposite poles, one instinct They could hardly be further apart. Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, 80, leads Latin America's biggest left-wing party. Benjamin Netanyahu , 77, heads the most right-wing government in Israel's history and is Donald Trump's closest ally abroad. One has spent the year denouncing American power in his hemisphere. The other spent it pulling American power into his. No side has reached a majority mark in the Israeli elections. Yet within a span of three days, both did what their critics thought they could not. Lula came from behind to win a fourth term on October 25. Two days later, Netanyahu turned an election night that the exit polls called a rout into something closer to a draw. Both have given master classes in the oldest skill in politics: Staying alive. Interestingly, US President Donald Trump had a stake in both contests. He openly endorsed Netanyahu, and he has long counted the Bolsonaro family as friends. His scoreline is 1-1. Lula: The comeback that stalled the Donroe Doctrine Brazil's first round on October 4 looked like the end. Flavio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of the jailed former president, took about 47% of the valid vote to Lula's 45%, defying final polls that had the president ahead. Lula admitted he had expected to win outright. The first survey afterwards gave Bolsonaro a six-point runoff lead. Three weeks later, the official count gave Lula 51.79% to 48.21%. The result halted a right-wing wave that had already delivered victories for Jose Antonio Kast in Chile, Abelardo de la Espriella in Colombia and Keiko Fujimori in Peru. How did he do it? Lula went back to the streets and went after the Bolsonaro family directly, raising its alleged links to militias. FlÃ¡vio had greeted his first-round lead by proclaiming the end of the Workers' Party era. It proved premature. Lula won the Brazil elections with over 4 million votes Trump's "Donroe Doctrine", his muscular update of the Monroe Doctrine, has split the hemisphere into friends and foes since the US seized Nicolas Maduro in January. Brazil was its biggest prize. Flavio had promised to join the US-backed Americas Shield security pact and to free his father. Lula has halted the Trump wagon. He is now the most powerful leftist still standing in Washington's way. The defeat has since turned into a spectacle. Flavio crossed into Argentina before flying to Miami with his family, after Trump offered them a way out. From the United States, he now casts himself as a victim of political persecution. Lula, meanwhile, is pressing ahead with his agenda. Netanyahu: Written off, not counted out In Israel, the script ran the other way. Almost every pre-election poll put Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc in front. When voting closed on October 27, the broadcasters' exit polls showed Eisenkot ahead by two or three seats, and his supporters partied in Tel Aviv. The count told another story. With about 90% of ballots tallied, Likud is the largest party with 26 seats, and Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc holds 53 seats to Eisenkot's 48. Turnout hit a historic high. Arab Israelis voted in record numbers, while Netanyahu's own base came out to defend him. Likud's response was telling: It accused the Arab parties of stealing the election. Trump, for his part, claimed his endorsement had turned the tide and hailed a come-from-behind performance. Letâs be clear: This is not an outright victory for Netanyahu. His bloc is eight seats short of a majority and down from 68 in the outgoing Knesset. But the opposition's arithmetic is worse. Arab parties won a record 19 seats, enough to give the anti-Netanyahu camp a majority, yet every Zionist opposition party except the Democrats has ruled out relying on them. Roughly 450,000 absentee ballots remain, official results are due on November 4, and coalition talks could drag on for months. If they fail, a unity government or yet another election both leave Netanyahu in office. Until then he stays on as caretaker, with full war powers, as a renewed war with Iran looms. The majority mark in Israel is 61 Netanyahu is already playing for time. He has assured his far-right partners. President Isaac Herzog has urged the parties to avoid another election and keep an open mind, while Washington says it has not decided whether to weigh in. What survivors share The two leaders from the opposite spectrum share a toolkit. Both have come back from the dead before: Lula from 580 days in prison, Netanyahu from defeats in 1999 and 2021 and a corruption trial that has shadowed him since 2020. Both turned Trump into fuel. Lula wrapped himself in sovereignty against American tariffs and threats; Netanyahu wore Trump's endorsement, which the US president now claims turned the tide. Both also owe something to opponents who could not close the deal. Flavio Bolsonaro let a two-point lead slip away in three weeks. Eisenkot's camp has an anti-Netanyahu majority in the new Knesset but no agreed way to use it. The art of survival The twin results say something about the moment. Voters on both continents are angry, yet anger has not produced clean breaks. Leaders with deep networks and long memories still know how to bring their people to the polls, and how to make rivals pay for hesitation. Lula's fight is over; he will be sworn in on January 1, 2027. Netanyahu's is not, and he may yet lose the coalition game. But no one should hurry to write his political obituary. title: In 2024, a Florida city began a $32 million project at its 209-acre Tucker Ranch preserve; two years later, it opened a 25.6-acre botanical and wellness park after finishing the work for $31 million
text: Florida city opens $31 million botanical and wellness park at 209-acre Tucker Ranch preserve (Image Credit: City Of Winter Garden) A former cattle ranch in Florida has gained a new purpose, bringing botanical gardens, outdoor fitness areas and wellness facilities together in a sprawling natural preserve. What began as a multimillion-dollar development project in 2024 has now opened to the public, offering residents a place to explore nature, learn about gardening and take part in health-focused activities. The city of Winter Garden officially opened the 25.6-acre Tucker Ranch Holistic Health and Wellness Park and Botanical Garden on October 23, 2026. According to the City of Winter Gardenâs official announcement, the project was completed for $31 million, below the planned budget of approximately $32 million. The new facilities form part of the larger 209-acre Tucker Ranch Park and Nature Preserve, expanding its recreational and educational offerings. A two-year project transforms part of the preserve Construction began with a groundbreaking ceremony on August 23, 2024. The 25.6-acre development was planned as an expansion of the existing nature preserve, whose first phase opened in 2018. The second phase was designed to offer more than a conventional public park. By bringing together nature, wellness facilities and educational spaces, Winter Garden aimed to create a setting where visitors could exercise, learn about nutrition and gardening, and spend time outdoors. The larger Tucker Ranch property is located at 100 Avalon Road. Its existing amenities include nature trails, a playground, picnic areas and a launch point for canoes and kayaks. Walking paths connect these facilities with the newly opened garden and wellness park. Botanical gardens and trails form the centrepiece The new park features a botanical garden containing ornamental plants, food-producing plants and varieties intended to attract pollinators. These collections provide a setting for visitors to explore the landscape while learning about plants and their role in the environment. The grounds also include nature paths, a boardwalk and a trail system with exercise stations. A covered pavilion extending over the water, along with a pond and fountain, adds spaces for visitors to pause and enjoy the surroundings. One distinctive feature is the historic West Orange Country Club entrance arch. The city preserved the structure and relocated it within the park to create a prominent entrance to the botanical garden. Together, the landscaped gardens and outdoor amenities are intended to make the site suitable for different types of visits, from daily walks and informal exercise to nature appreciation and family outings. Retreat centre and teaching kitchen expand activities Beyond its outdoor facilities, the development includes a 5,000-square-foot Retreat Center with an indoor venue and screened patio. The space is intended to accommodate classes, community programmes and other organised activities. Another facility, The Ranch House, includes a demonstration kitchen, outdoor patio and fireplace. The kitchen can support educational activities centred on cooking, nutrition and food preparation. Edible Learning Gardens provide opportunities for visitors to explore gardening techniques and understand how food can be grown at home or in community settings. These facilities complement the botanical garden by connecting environmental education with everyday health and lifestyle practices. The city has also worked with local health and wellness organisations, including AdventHealth, Orlando Health and Healthy West Orange, to support the broader vision for the property. The aim is to make wellness accessible through a combination of movement, learning, social engagement and time in nature. Historic property gains a new community role Tucker Ranch has a history that predates its development as a public preserve. The property was once associated with the West Orange Country Club, which operated in the early 20th century. During the Second World War, the area also served as Camp Kent, where radar-related testing took place. The Tucker family later operated a cattle ranch on the land, and Tucker's Ranch Campground opened in 1969. The city later gained ownership of the property, paving the way for its development as a public preserve. The new botanical and wellness park builds on that history while giving the land a broader public purpose. Rather than replacing the natural setting with a conventional recreation complex, the project combines constructed amenities with gardens, water features and existing trails. Free public access to the expanded park The grand opening took place on October 23, 2026, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony and an opportunity for visitors to tour the new facilities. Admission is free, and the park is open daily. According to the city's published schedule, Tucker Ranch operates from 8 am to 6 pm between March and October, and from 8 am to 5 pm between November and February. Parking and restrooms are available on site. With the second phase complete, Winter Garden has expanded a 209-acre preserve with facilities intended to serve families, nature enthusiasts and people interested in outdoor wellness. The $31 million project brings botanical exploration, exercise, gardening education and community programming together in one public setting.

title: Ashutosh Dixit, a strong advocate of Atmanirbharta initiatives who played key roles in Kargil War & Op Sindoor, takes charge as 29th IAF chief
text: NEW DELHI: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, a strong advocate for Aatmanirbharta initiatives in the defence sector and played key roles in the Kargil War as well as Op Sindoor, on Saturday took charge as the 29th Indian Air Force (IAF) chief. He succeeds Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, who superannuated after 42 years of distinguished service to the nation. On Saturday, outgoing IAF chief ACM Amar Preet Singh laid a wreath at the National War Memorial in New Delhi and was accorded a ceremonial guard of honour at the Race Course Air Force Station before he handed over the baton to Dixit. Over a career spanning four decades, ACM Dixit has rich experience across diverse domains such as operations, flight testing, capability development and joint staff assignments. An accomplished fighter pilot, qualified flying instructor and experimental test pilot, ACM Dixit has over 3,300 hours of flying experience on a wide range of aircraft, including Mirage-2000, various MiG variants, Jaguar and several transport aircraft. Widely recognised for his contribution to the modernisation of the IAF, he was instrumental in finalising the Jaguar and MiG-27 upgrade projects and in the completion of the initial operational clearance (IOC) and final operational clearance (FOC) activities of the LCA Mk-I Tejas. Watch 94 Years Of The IAF: The Road Ahead For India's Air Arm His operational command assignments include command of a Mirage-2000 squadron, a forward base support unit in the western sector and Air Force Station Bidar, a premier fighter training base of the IAF. The Air Officer has served as Air Defence Commander at Southern Air Command, Senior Air Staff Officer at South Western Air Command and Deputy Chief of the Air Staff, steering key capability development and procurement initiatives. He subsequently commanded Central Air Command as Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief and later served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee during Operation Sindoor . Prior to assuming charge as Chief of the Air Staff, he served as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff. An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, ACM was commissioned into the fighter stream of the IAF on Dec 6, 1986. Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is an accomplished graduate of the Defence Services Command and Staff College, Bangladesh, and National Defence College, New Delhi. He is a recipient of the Vayu Sena Medal, Vishisht Seva Medal, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal and Param Vishisht Seva Medal in recognition of his distinguished service to the nation.

title: CBI adds charges carrying life term in bank recruitment racket probe
text: Mumbai: CBI has invoked stringent charges of forgery of valuable security and provisions of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in its probe into an alleged impersonation racket involving 135 candidates selected through Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) recruitment examinations. The forgery charge attracts a maximum punishment of life imprisonment. A special court on Friday took on record CBIâs intimation to invoke additional penal provisions. It is alleged that at least 180 such aspirants cleared and are employed in various banks. Sections 3, 4 and 5 are offences of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act that are related to prohibition of unfair means, disruption and criminal conspiracy. When invoked with the penal provisions, Section 10 prescribes imprisonment of up to five years and a Rs 10 lakh fine for individual offenders, while Section 11 is related to organised crime syndicates with a harsher maximum penalty of up to 10 years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 1 crore. âHaving considered the submissions and the record, it appears that based upon the facts revealed during the course of investigation, the provisions as aforementioned are invokedâ¦,â the judge said. The case was registered on Aug 20, 2026, on the complaint of the Head, Research and Development, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, Mumbai. The FIR was lodged against Ashish Avinash and 134 others for alleged fraudulent selection through impersonation for appointments to different posts in various banks in examinations conducted by IBPS between 2020 and 2024. According to CBI, field verification of the biometrics of suspected impersonators during the investigation revealed that accused Rajeev Ranjan , Vishwa Bhaskar, Abhishek Kumar alias Roshan and Manish Kumar had allegedly appeared in place of the actual candidates at different stages of the recruitment process. The agency also examined invigilators Sagar Gupta and Sakshi Chhipa, who were posted at examination centres in Lucknow and Ajmer, Rajasthan, respectively. CBI told the court that the impersonators had allegedly signed and provided sample handwriting on admit cards in the names of the original candidates in the presence of the invigilators. On this basis, the investigating officer sought to invoke Section 467 of the IPC, which deals with forgery of valuable security, will or authority to make or transfer valuable security. The agency further submitted that the respondent candidate arrayed as accused No 129 had allegedly secured a job after one Sonu Kumar appeared in his place on Aug 30, 2024, and Sept 29, 2024. On account of this allegation, CBI sought to invoke Sections 3, 4 and 5 read with Sections 10 and 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. title: Six Gujarat RUPPs report over â¹2,692cr in donations over five years
text: Gandhinagar : Six registered unrecognised political parties (RUPPs) in Gujarat reported total donations running into hundreds of crores of rupees over five financial years from 2020-21 to 2024-25, according to data compiled by the independent election watchdog Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) on the partiesâ income, expenditure, donations and electoral performance. Over the past month, Gujarat Police have registered four FIRs against such parties for allegedly receiving massive funds, routing them back to donors in cash via shell entities, and charging a 2% to 10% commission to facilitate tax evasion. According to ADRâs compilation, Bharatiya Rashtriya Janata Dal reported total donations of Rs 0.36 crore in 2020-21, Rs 189 crore in 2021-22, Rs 576.5 crore in 2022-23, Rs 191.6 crore in 2023-24 and Rs 198.8 crore in 2024-25. Its reported donations over the five years totalled Rs 1,156.1 crore. New India United Party reported total donations of Rs 407.5 crore in 2022-23 and Rs 291.6 crore in 2024-25. Its total donation figures for 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2023-24 were unavailable in the compiled data. The partyâs reported cumulative total was Rs 699.1 crore. Swatantra Abhivyakti Party reported nil donations in 2020-21, Rs 75.9 crore in 2021-22 and Rs 395.4 crore in 2022-23. Its total donation figures for 2023-24 and 2024-25 were unavailable. The cumulative figure reported in the document was Rs 75.9 crore. Satyavadi Rakshak Party reported total donations of nil in 2021-22, Rs 85.7 crore in 2022-23 and Rs 330.6 crore in 2023-24. Figures for 2020-21 and 2024-25 were unavailable. Its reported cumulative total was Rs 416.2 crore. Saurashtra Janata Paksh reported zero donations in 2020-21, Rs 131.3 crore in 2021-22, Rs 53.3 crore in 2022-23, Rs 15.9 crore in 2023-24 and Rs 10.8 crore in 2024-25. title: Chandigarh couple pays Rs 62.7 lakh, nearly 95% of flat cost, but builder repeatedly delays possession for 2 years, he then stops monthly compensation and issues possession letter despite apartment lacking fire safety certificate. Now, consumer commission orders refund with 12% interest and Rs 1.1 lakh compensation and costs
text: (AI image) A State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered a builder to refund â¹62.7 lakh with interest to a couple. CHANDIGARH: A real estate firm and its two directors have been directed to refund Rs 62.7 lakh with 12% annual interest to a Zirakpur homebuyer couple after repeatedly delaying possession of their flat, stopping monthly compensation and issuing a possession letter despite the apartment lacking a fire safety certificate. The State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, UT Chandigarh, also ordered the builder to pay Rs 75,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 35,000 towards litigation costs within 30 days, holding the firm guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices. Saurabh Verma and his wife, Puja Rani, booked a 1,590-square-foot apartment for Rs 66.5 lakh in October 2022, with possession originally scheduled for October 31, 2023. They paid Rs 62.7 lakh, including Rs 40.1 lakh through a home loan, but the developer failed to deliver the flat within the agreed period. The builder subsequently extended the possession deadline three times, in September 2023, August 2024 and August 2025. The revised deadlines were November 2024, July 2025 and December 31, 2025. The firm initially paid the couple Rs 30,000 per month as compensation for the delay, but stopped making the payments after a year. The commission directed that the compensation paid between November 2023 and November 2024 be adjusted against the final refund. Possession letter issued despite missing fire safety certificate The couple alleged that the builder demanded additional money for finishing work despite the slow pace of construction. They claimed the firm threatened to cancel the contract and charge 24% interest if they failed to make the payments. On September 27, 2025, the developer issued a possession letter, which the buyers refused to accept, citing incomplete construction and the absence of mandatory statutory approvals. An RTI response dated January 2, 2026, confirmed that the apartment lacked a fire safety certificate, according to the complaint. The commission observed that issuing a possession letter without the required statutory clearances did not establish that a residential unit was fit for occupation. It also noted that the builder's defence was struck off on April 16, 2026, after the firm failed to file its written reply within the prescribed 45-day period. Buyers cannot be made to wait indefinitely Relying on Supreme Court precedents, the commission held that homebuyers could not be compelled to wait indefinitely for possession or accept an incomplete apartment. "The obligation of a builder is not merely to construct a structure or issue a letter describing possession as offered; it is to deliver the contracted residential unit within the stipulated period, in a habitable condition and in conformity with the applicable statutory requirements," the commission observed. It held that repeated delays, discontinuation of compensation and demands for additional funds amounted to material deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The commission also highlighted that the couple had paid nearly 95% of the flat's total cost, leaving a substantial portion of their financial resources tied up in a property whose lawful and habitable possession had not been established. The builder and its two directors have been directed to refund Rs 62.7 lakh with 12% annual interest calculated from the respective dates of deposit. title: Iran to shift uranium stockpile abroad, reopen Hormuz within 7 days under draft deal: Report
text: Iran-US draft proposes uranium transfer, Hormuz reopening within 7 days NEW DELHI: A preliminary framework for negotiations between the United States and Iran proposes transferring Tehran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium to a third country or reducing its enrichment levels, alongside reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping within seven days of an initial understanding, Al Arabiya English reported on Saturday. The draft framework, which was obtained exclusively by the news platform, also identifies China as a potential guarantor to ensure the implementation and sustainability of any agreement. It proposes holding direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran in Doha instead of Istanbul. Under the proposed arrangement, Iran would undertake commitments on its nuclear programme and maritime security in exchange for US steps to ease sanctions, blockades and other economic restrictions. The framework also envisages an independent verification mechanism to assess compliance before each phase of implementation. This would ensure that neither side makes substantial concessions without corresponding and independently verifiable commitments from the other. Watch Trumpâs Cheesecake Factory Controversy EXPLODES as Kimmel Launches Fresh Attack A separate dispute-resolution mechanism involving mediators and guarantor countries has also been proposed to address delays or violations and prevent a fresh escalation of military tensions, according to Al Arabiya English. Qatar steps up diplomatic outreach Diplomatic efforts to revive a ceasefire between Washington and Tehran gathered pace on Friday, with a Qatari delegation arriving in the Iranian capital for consultations, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported. The delegation, led by a senior adviser to Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, arrived on Friday morning and was coordinating its efforts with the United States. Meanwhile, a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei was reportedly delivered by Qatari envoys. The communication was welcomed in Tehran for proposing a fresh diplomatic pathway to prevent further American military strikes, according to reports. Trump says US in no hurry to end war The diplomatic developments come amid US President Donald Trump's assertion that Washington is in no hurry to end its conflict with Iran, describing the hostilities as "not a typical war". Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump claimed that Tehran remained interested in negotiations but was facing domestic financial difficulties, including an inability to pay military personnel and law enforcement officers. âThere are talks. They want to talk. They keep talking,â Trump told reporters. âBut look, they're not paying their soldiers, they're not paying their police. They're in a lot of trouble. And we have time, frankly. It's a war, but it's not a typical war; we've been there for seven months,â he added. Trump also played down the financial burden of the military campaign, claiming that Washington's expenditure on the conflict was relatively low and had been offset by gains elsewhere. âWe're spending very little money, relatively speaking. I heard somebody say, you're spending money. I said, well, any money we spent, we've more than made up for in a place called Venezuela, like by 10 times...â he said. However, he did not provide figures to substantiate his claim about recovering the cost of the military campaign through Venezuela. Despite expressing confidence that the US had time on its side, Trump has repeatedly raised the possibility of renewed military action against Iran. He previously referred to the prospect of launching âanother little Epic Furyâ, a reference to the initial US military operation against Tehran, while also suggesting that a âbig and goodâ agreement could still be reached. Turkey also engages Washington Parallel diplomatic efforts continued as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the sidelines of a G20 ministerial gathering in the United States on Friday. According to Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency, the discussions covered the ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran, regional developments and bilateral relations. The meeting followed a telephone conversation between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Trump earlier in the week. During the call, Ankara conveyed its concerns over maritime routes and expressed support for diplomatic initiatives to reduce regional tensions. The proposed framework comes amid continuing differences between Washington and Tehran over Iran's nuclear programme, sanctions and the US blockade of Iranian ports. title: Princess Dianaâs homelessness charity now supports more than 15,000 young people each year, with 69% moving towards independent living
text: PC: The Passage Homelessness charities often work with young people at a point when finding somewhere safe to stay is only the beginning of a much longer process. Securing accommodation does not necessarily mean someone is ready to manage a home, return to education or find work without continued assistance. Centrepoint, the UK charity associated with Princess Diana and now supported by her son, Prince William, works with young people facing these challenges. Its services have expanded considerably since the organisation began in London in 1969. As reported by Centrepoint UK, in 2024/25, it and its partner organisations supported more than 15,000 young people, with its latest figures offering an insight into the help provided and what happens when they leave. Princess Dianaâs homelessness charity reaches 15,000 young people in a year Centrepoint began in 1969 in the basement of a church in Soho, London. The organisation was established to provide a place for young people experiencing homelessness, at a time when the support available to them was limited. The scale of its current work is reflected in its housing provision. Reportedly, Centrepoint operates 90 supported housing services across the UK, with more than 800 bed spaces available to young people. These services are intended to offer more than temporary shelter, giving residents access to support as they work towards greater stability. In 2024/25, the charity and its partner organisations reached more than 15,000 young people. The organisation's 2024/25 figures cover several areas of its work, including housing, education and emotional wellbeing. One measure concerns the experience of people using its services: 83% of young people surveyed said they were satisfied with the overall support Centrepoint provided. Its therapeutic services also recorded a positive response. Among young people who engaged with the charity's therapeutic services team, 93% reported that the support had made a positive difference. Education and employment preparation form another part of its work. During the year, young people receiving assistance from Skills and Employability Trainers achieved 379 certificates and qualifications. These provide a measure of progress in building skills, although the charity's work extends beyond formal learning. How Centrepoint helps young people take the next step after homelessness Moving out of supported accommodation is an important stage for people who have experienced homelessness, but leaving a service does not automatically mean someone is prepared to live independently. Centrepoint assesses whether young people have the practical and personal readiness needed to manage that transition. For 2024/25, the charity reported that 69% of young people who left its services were ready to move into independent living. The figure offers an indication of how many had reached that stage when their support ended. It also reflects the organisation's emphasis on helping residents develop the ability to manage their next accommodation arrangements rather than simply finding them somewhere else to stay. Not every young person experiencing homelessness is already living in supported accommodation or receiving help from a housing service. Some need information about their rights, somewhere to turn for emotional support or guidance on finding suitable accommodation. Centrepoint's helpline is intended to provide that point of contact. During 2024/25, it assisted 5,166 young people, offering advice on housing rights, emotional support and access to supported accommodation. The service gives young people a way to seek help even when they are not already part of the charity's housing network. Princess Diana's connection with the charity Princess Diana's association with homelessness charities also helped bring greater public attention to the issue. Her involvement with âThe Passageâ, another organisation working with people experiencing homelessness, became particularly significant for her family. In 1993, she took Prince William to visit The Passage for the first time. The visit introduced him to the experiences of people who relied on homelessness services and became an important part of his later involvement in the sector. The Passage has since described Diana's influence as part of the inspiration behind William's continued interest in the issue. William became Royal Patron of The Passage in February 2019. He is also Patron of Centrepoint, continuing a family connection with organisations working to support people without secure housing. Prince William's work to address homelessness William's involvement has extended beyond individual charity visits. Through Homewards, a five-year programme launched by The Royal Foundation, he has been working with organisations and communities to demonstrate how homelessness can be prevented and addressed. The Passage has a role in the initiative, contributing experience from its frontline services and helping inform longer-term approaches. The programme brings together organisations working in different areas, recognising that housing insecurity can involve a range of practical and social challenges. The royal family's association with these charities has developed over several decades, from Diana's visits to William's current patronages and public work. You use AI every day. title: Opposition trying to foment anarchy amid global crisis, says PM Modi
text: PM Modi accuses opposition of spreading rumours and creating panic over Iran war, alleges bid to foment anarchy and defame him BHILDI (BANASKANTHA): Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday accused the opposition of rumour-mongering and creating panic at a time when the country was unitedly trying to deal with the crisis triggered by the Iran war and the wider Middle East conflict. He alleged that its aim was to foment anarchy across the country and defame him. Addressing a gathering in Bhildi, Banaskantha, after inaugurating the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBBRC) and launching development projects worth Rs 14,000 crore, Modi said the country was united in working towards the goal of a Viksit Bharat, but some people were unhappy with its progress. âToday every citizen in the country is working towards the dream of Viksit Bharat. But, unfortunately, there are some people who are not liking this. They want the country to remain steeped in crisis. In fact, they rejoice when the country is in trouble,â Modi said. He also asserted that he would continue serving the people until his last breath. The remarks came days after Congress president Mallikarjun Khargeâs comment suggesting Modiâs imminent exit triggered a political controversy for his choice of words. Without directly referring to it, Modi declared: âJeevan ke antim kshan tak janta ki seva main hi juta rahunga (I will continue to serve the people until my last breath). â Referring to the Iran war and the wider Middle East crisis, he accused his political opponents of spreading fears about shortages of fertilisers and cooking gas, and disrupting the lives of ordinary citizens. âWhen India is unitedly striving to fight the effects of this war, they are spread rumours that farmers wonât get fertilizer, women wonât get gas to cook and children wonât be able to go to school. They vitiated the atmosphere,â he said. âTheir plan was to incite anarchy across the country, solely to defame me,â he told the gathering. Modi said govt had ensured that farmers continued to receive fertilisers despite a surge in global prices and the cost of chemicals used in their manufacture. âI had promised that I would stand firmly by your side. Even though the conflict continues, we have ensured that there is no shortage of fertilisers for our farmers,â he said. âGlobally, a bag of urea costs as much as Rs 3,000, yet Indian farmers receive it for less than Rs 300. The government took this entire burden on itself,â he said. He added that while the global price of a bag of diammonium phosphate (DAP) had crossed Rs 5,000, Indian farmers were receiving it for Rs 1,350. title: Renukaswamy murder case: Darshan case witness says he left shed before alleged murder; claims he does not know what happened later
text: Picture Credit: Facebook The 2024 Renukaswamy murder case involving Kannada superstar Darshan and his friend Pavithra Gowda saw a huge development as an employee of the shed where the alleged murder took place turned hostile on Wednesday. As per the latest updates, he told the court that he did not know what happened at the shed where Renukaswamy was allegedly murdered. Prime witness turns hostile in Darshan case According to a report by TNN Bengaluru, Darshan and Pavithra appeared before the court through video conference from Central Prison in Parappana Agrahara. Witness says he did not know what happened at shed During the hearing, the witness, Puneeth MJ, who worked at the Pattanagere shed, shared that three men were already present at the shed when he arrived for work on June 8, 2024. According to the prosecution, the alleged murder took place between 12:30 pm and 6:30 pm that day. Puneeth also told the court that five more people arrived in a car later. However, he said he did not know who they were and could not identify the accused who appeared through video conference. He claimed that he left the shed around 6:30 pm to travel to Male Mahadeshwara Hills after having food. A few other employees, including a security guard, were still there when he left. He told the court that he did not know what happened afterwards. Puneeth further testified that he learnt about the murder through news reports on June 10. He said the police contacted him the same day and asked him to visit the police station. He later travelled to his hometown near Kanakapura and then to Hassan. He also told the court that he changed his mobile phone and purchased a basic handset. Special Public Prosecutor Prasanna P Kumar said Puneeth was being cross-examined over his testimony and the prosecution's allegation that he had turned hostile. The court adjourned the hearing until Thursday. Darshan seeks physiotherapy for back pain Meanwhile, Darshan informed the court that he was suffering from back pain and requested physiotherapy. title: Rajasthan orders verification of Rs 3,000cr MGNREGA dues pending with Centre
text: Jaipur: Rajasthan govt has ordered block-level verification of nearly Rs 3,000 crore in pending material component payments under MGNREGA for 2024 and 2025, which are yet to be released by the Centre. The rural development department has directed officials to verify the outstanding amounts and submit reports, which will be consolidated by the state govt and forwarded to the Centre to seek release of the funds. An official of the rural development department said the block-level verification has already started. âOnce we receive reports from all the districts, we will send them to the Centre. The pending material component payments for 2024 and 2025 are being verified at the blocks,â the official said. The verification comes amid concerns over the impact of the delayed payments on development works in gram panchayats. In a representation to chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma, Sarpanch Sangh Rajasthan and outgoing panchayat administrators said around Rs 3,200 crore due under the material component of MGNREGA had remained unpaid for nearly 30 months. The association said the delay had affected development work in most gram panchayats, while material suppliers had disrupted supplies and were holding public representatives responsible for the pending payments. It urged the chief minister to ensure early release of the funds to help resume development work and ease the financial difficulties faced by gram panchayats. Even though the Centre introduced the Viksit BharatâGuarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Grameen), or VB-G RAM-G, replacing MGNREGS in July, material component payments under the earlier scheme remain pending in Rajasthan for two years. Meanwhile, the state govt has written to the Centre seeking an increase in the annual employment guarantee under VB-G RAM-G from 125 to 150 days in drought-affected districts, a rural development department official said. The request comes after the state govt on Sunday declared 80 tehsils across 14 districts drought-affected for the 2026 kharif season, citing deficient rainfall and adverse crop conditions.
