title: OREAT upholds Rs 90L penalty on Puri developer, sets aside demolition
text: Bhubaneswar: Odisha Real Estate Appellate Tribunal (OREAT) has upheld a Rs 90 lakh penalty imposed on a city-based real estate developer for deviating from the sanctioned plan of its housing project in Puri but set aside a demolition direction issued earlier by Odisha Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Orera). In its recent order, the tribunal held that the developer had constructed a G+10 commercial-cum-residential building despite having approval for a G+7 residential project at Sipasarubali. The deviation was challenged at Orera in 2024. The tribunal said that the revised plan had never received final approval from Puri-Konark Development Authority (PKDA), and that mandatory clearances, including an Airports Authority of India NOC and pollution-related approvals, had not been obtained. The tribunal agreed with Oreraâs finding that the promoter violated the provisions of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, by carrying out development contrary to the sanctioned plan. It also upheld the Rs 90 lakh penalty, observing that the amount constituted only around 0.54% of the projectâs estimated cost of Rs 166 crore. However, OREAT ruled that Orera exceeded its jurisdiction by directing PKDA to demolish the unauthorised portions of the building. âThe regulatorâs powers under Sections 35 to 38 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act do not extend to ordering a development authority to carry out demolition,â it said, adding that âany such action would have to be taken independently under ODA Actâ. A significant development recorded during the appeal was that PKDA had regularised the existing G+10 structure through an order issued on May 21, after collecting compounding fees and other charges from the developer. While taking note of the regularisation, the tribunal referred to a series of Supreme Court judgments on unauthorised constructions. OREAT observed that courts have consistently held that illegal structures should not ordinarily be condoned, and that authorities must act against violations of approved building plans. The tribunal said the validity of PKDAâs regularisation order would have to be examined in light of these principles laid down by the apex court. title: Jeff Bezos' $1 million grant is helping formerly incarcerated young people in Atlanta build farming businesses across 30 Black-owned farms and create 40 jobs
text: A $1 million grant from Jeff Bezos' Bezos Earth Fund is supporting Gangstas to Growers, an Atlanta-based organisation that uses agriculture to create employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. Awarded in July 2023, the funding is intended to expand regenerative agricultural production across 30 farms on Black-owned land and create 40 new jobs. The initiative also aims to strengthen local food systems and generate economic activity in West Atlanta. By combining practical farming experience with business education and mentorship, the programme seeks to help participants develop marketable skills and explore pathways towards economic independence while supporting Black-owned farms and community-led food production. How Jeff Bezos' $1 million grant is supporting Atlanta's formerly incarcerated youth Gangstas to Growers, also known as G2G, is an Atlanta-based social enterprise founded by Abiodun Henderson. The organisation uses agriculture as a way to provide employment, entrepreneurship and personal-development opportunities to at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. The initiative works with Black-owned farms around Atlanta, giving participants opportunities to learn agricultural skills through practical projects. Its approach combines farming with mentorship, business education and personal development, with the broader aim of addressing barriers to employment and reducing recidivism, which refers to returning to criminal behaviour or the criminal justice system after an earlier offence or period of incarceration. The Bezos Earth Fund awarded the $1 million grant in July 2023 to help the organisation expand its agricultural training and infrastructure. According to the fund, G2G plans to expand regenerative agricultural production across 30 farms on Black-owned land and create 40 new jobs for at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. How the programme combines farming with employment and training Participants learn practical agricultural skills, including seeding, growing, harvesting and composting. They receive opportunities to work on projects at Black-owned farms while gaining experience that can help them explore employment and entrepreneurship. The programme extends beyond agricultural instruction. Its curriculum also includes business education, mentorship, yoga, life coaching and arts classes. These activities are designed to help participants develop confidence, leadership abilities and skills that can be applied to different career paths. A December 2024 report by Georgia Public Broadcasting (GPB) documented how participants engage with the programme. It highlighted the experiences of young people who were developing agricultural skills while considering different professional ambitions. Not everyone intends to pursue farming as a full-time career. One participant featured in the report planned to pursue videography while continuing to grow plants at home. Another wanted to develop a business focused on helping people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity. Gangstas to Growers participants take part in hands-on farming activities in Atlanta. (Gangstas to Growers / Bezos Earth Fund) How Gangstas to Growers is helping participants build businesses Beyond providing agricultural training, G2G aims to help participants develop businesses through worker-owned cooperatives. The model gives graduates opportunities to participate in collective ownership and build enterprises connected to local food production. One example is Sweet Sol, a hot sauce business associated with the organisation's graduates. Participants grow and harvest ingredients used to make the product, while the cooperative model connects agricultural production with food processing, product development and sales. According to G2G, proceeds support young people, the programme and Black-owned farms around Atlanta. The initiative demonstrates how agricultural training can lead to opportunities beyond farm work, including developing products and participating in small businesses. The organisation also works towards strengthening community ownership of food-related enterprises, allowing participants to explore business opportunities while contributing to the local economy. Part of a $7.9 million investment in Atlanta's green spaces The $1 million grant was part of the Bezos Earth Fund's announcement of $7.9 million in funding for urban greening projects in Atlanta on July 17, 2023. The funding supported nine projects intended to improve access to green spaces and strengthen environmental conditions in underserved communities. The wider investment included initiatives involving urban farms, community gardens, native plants, wildlife habitats and agricultural workforce development. It formed part of the fund's $400 million Greening America's Cities initiative, which aims to improve equitable access to urban green spaces through 2030. Another recipient, On Da Farm, received $1 million to support urban farming, native plant cultivation, wildlife habitats and agricultural workforce development. Its plans included training 40 new farmers and 12 farmer apprentices, alongside producing food for local families through its weekly farmers' market. Gangstas to Growers' work fits into this broader strategy by connecting environmental sustainability with employment opportunities, food access and community economic development. What the organisation has achieved so far Gangstas to Growers reports that its work has resulted in 5,000 pounds of food being harvested, 25 Black-owned farms being serviced and 20 programme graduates. These figures appear in the organisation's published impact summary and reflect its reported activities. Its website does not clearly specify the reporting period for each figure. The initiative has also received independent coverage. In December 2024, GPB reported on a graduating cohort, documenting how participants were developing agricultural skills and considering different career paths through the programme. The Bezos Earth Fund's grant announcement identifies expanding production across 30 Black-owned farms and creating 40 jobs as objectives of the investment. The available reporting does not establish whether these specific targets have been fully achieved. Through agricultural training, paid work and business development, Gangstas to Growers is seeking to create economic opportunities for young people who face barriers to employment while supporting Black-owned farms and strengthening Atlanta's local food system. title: GVMC records 56.3% turnout, with core city areas lagging behind peripheral zones in voter participation
text: Visakhapatnam : The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) election recorded a voter turnout of 56.32%, significantly lower than the 59.41% polled in 2021 and the 64% to 80% recorded across assembly constituencies within GVMC limits in the 2024 general elections. The turnout, nearly 15 percentage points below the 2024 assembly election levels in some areas, has triggered speculation among political parties over its possible impact on the results, which will be declared on Tuesday. While low polling has been a recurring feature of municipal elections in Visakhapatnam, parties had expected a better response, given growing political awareness and increased access to information through technology. The core city areas once again recorded lower polling than the peripheral zones, following a pattern similar to the 2024 assembly elections. Zone-wise turnout ranged from 49.71% to 66.27%. Bheemili topped the list with 66.27%, followed by Anakapalli (65.6%), Aganampudi (62.08%) and Gajuwaka (60.9%). West zone recorded 58.97%, while Pendurthi and Madhurawada registered 55.12% and 55.07%, respectively. East and South zones polled 54.21% and 52.61%, respectively. North zone recorded the lowest turnout at 49.71%. A similar pattern was evident in the 2024 assembly elections, when the four core city constituencies recorded relatively low polling. Vizag South registered 63.42%, the lowest, followed by North (64.63%), East (68.5%) and West (69.78%). All four constituencies fell short of the stateâs overall assembly election turnout of 80.66%. Among the seven assembly constituencies in Visakhapatnam district, only Pendurthi and Bheemili crossed the 70% mark, recording 74% and 76%, respectively. Anakapalli registered nearly 80%. The subdued turnout has left both major political parties assessing its possible implications for the mayoral contest and corporator results. The TDP is confident of securing the mayorâs post and a majority of the corporator seats. The YSRCP, meanwhile, is banking on cross-voting to win the mayoral election, while hoping to secure 40 to 50 of the 120 corporator seats. YSRCP leaders believe the candidature of MLC and party state womenâs wing president Varudu Kalyani has helped the party attract urban, educated voters and professionals. They expect this support to translate into a narrow victory in the mayoral contest. The TDP, on the other hand, is banking on its mayoral candidate, young corporator Mukka Sravani, arguing that her five years of work among the public will give the party an advantage. Political analysts attribute the low turnout to a combination of urban voter apathy, lacklustre campaigning and the absence of a strong political wave or compelling local issues. The delayed finalisation of candidates and release of manifestos also left parties with limited time to reach out to voters. Cyclone Arnab further disrupted normal life and electioneering during the crucial final days of campaigning, potentially affecting voter mobilisation. Another factor cited by observers is the cityâs growing migrant population. Many of those who have moved to Visakhapatnam in recent years may not yet have developed strong political connections with local leaders or the same level of engagement with civic affairs as long-time residents. Low-key contests in several wards and inadequate voter outreach may have further contributed to the subdued response. title: Former media CEO Nic Jones left a decades-long career for bus driving; eight months later, he called himself a fulfilled and happy bus driver
text: AI Representation: Former media executive Nic Jones left his corporate career to become a bus driver, a change he described as fulfilling and rewarding after eight months on the job. Image credits: Chatgpt A successful career can bring professional recognition, financial security and opportunities to lead, yet those achievements do not always guarantee personal satisfaction. Nic Jones, a former media executive in Australia, left the corporate world after a long career in media and music to pursue his lifelong interest in buses, becoming a bus driver in Sydney. Jones began driving for the transport operator Keolis Downer in April 2024. In a profile published by Australasian Bus & Coach magazine in December 2024, he said he loved the feeling of helping people and valued the camaraderie among his fellow drivers. His move offers a different picture of career development from the usual climb up the corporate ladder. Nic Jonesâs dream of driving a double-decker bus since he was five Jones told Australasian Bus & Coach that one of his earliest memories, growing up in England, was sitting with his mother on a bus into town and wanting to sit behind the driver of the double-decker to see how he drove. He said he was less interested in where they were going than in watching the driver. After finishing university in the UK, he also worked as a long-distance lorry driver for a year before deciding he needed a âreal job. â For the best part of 40 years, the magazine reports, Jones held executive positions in media and music, including CEO of an ASX-listed company an most recently, of the live music platform Moshcam. His Advertising Week APAC biography lists senior roles at Yahoo and Vevo, where he was chief revenue officer. He said he often joked with his family on holidays that he might one day become a bus driver. The 2024 funding loss and the decision to return to a childhood dream The profile reports that the funding Jonesâs business needed fell through at the start of 2024, forcing him to step away from it. His fatherâs death in the UK that January added to the setback and Jones decided the best way to rebound was to return to the dream he had first had as a five-year-old. He said he wanted to recapture his purpose in life and try something different and although Uber driving was an option, he chose buses because of the community-minded side of his personality. He earned his MR/HGV licence and applied to become a bus driver and in April he began driving for Keolis Downer, a public transport operator, on Sydneyâs Northern Beaches. The magazine adds that Jones is already wondering whether he could add value to Keolis Downer and the wider bus industry and he said he would be interested in operations work if the chance came up, though first he wants to master driving a bus. Driving for Keolis Downer on Sydneyâs Northern Beaches from April 2024 Starting the job brought difficulties. The magazine reports that Jones was nervous before his first day with Keolis Downer, but that driving gradually became second nature and he said a bus is not an easy vehicle to drive. He added that the public are, for the most part, delightful, that the drivers are an incredibly close group and that his biggest worry had been that he would not find his people. Buses navigate Sydney's busy streets, highlighting the concentration and responsibility involved in passenger transport. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons The description of an October 2024 episode of the Future Squared podcast says Jones discusses how driving buses and working with people each day gives him a sense of meaning he can see. He also wrote on LinkedIn that he loves feeling that he is working in and for the community. What Jones said about purpose and privilege in late 2024 By the time of the magazineâs December 2024 profile, about eight months after he started, Jones said he loved driving and helping people. His experience suggests that career satisfaction can come without a high-profile role or a high-status title. His story does not imply that everyone should leave an established career, or that bus driving automatically brings happiness and the Future Squared episode description notes that Jones himself addresses the view that leaving a well-paying job is a choice open to only a few. Still, his case points to another way of approaching career change, since some people may find work satisfaction that does not involve climbing the corporate ladder and for Jones, the move brought him closer to the dream he had held since he was five. title: Previous Delhi govt approved DSIIDC's liquor booking app to ensure transparency in retail sales, says official
text: Initially, the app was compatible only with Android devices. (AI Image) NEW DELHI: The Delhi Liquor Booking app was approved by the previous government in 2024 to ensure transparency and prevent brand pushing in retail liquor sales, the Delhi State Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC) said on Wednesday. The app was launched by DSIIDC in November 2025 after the required trials, allowing customers to book liquor online and collect it from the corporation's retail vends, officials said. "In order to ensure transparency, digital governance and avoid brand pushing, the Delhi Liquor Booking app was rolled out by DSIIDC in November 2025. Earlier, approval was granted for developing the app by DSIIDC Management in December 2024. A work order for developing the app was issued on January 2, 2025," a senior DSIIDC officer said. Initially, the app was compatible only with Android devices. To extend the facility to iOS users and ensure platform neutrality, DSIIDC launched a QR code-enabled microsite on September 6. During the 2025-26 financial year, the app recorded 3,629 transactions, with liquor sales worth around Rs 13 lakh. In the current financial year, liquor worth around Rs 30 lakh has been sold through 10,730 transactions so far, officials said. Customers can register on the app to check the availability of liquor stocks, place orders and make digital payments. The facility is intended to prevent brand pushing by allowing customers to select their preferred products online. Once an order is confirmed and verified, customers must collect the purchased bottle from the designated store. Home delivery is not available through the app, officials said. Customers can cancel their orders before collecting the purchased bottle, they added. Users must also verify that they are above the legal drinking age of 25 years to use the app, officials said. The initiative also aims to reduce crowds outside liquor stores, which can sometimes lead to law and order situations, they added. Four Delhi government corporations operate more than 700 retail liquor stores across the city. However, online booking is currently available only at over 200 vends run by DSIIDC. Under Excise rules, an individual can possess up to nine litres of whisky and 18 litres of beer. Liquor that has been sold or collected by a consumer cannot be returned, according to the rules. title: Tech glitches hit A to B khata upgrade
text: Bengaluru: Thousands of property owners waiting to upgrade from B-khata to A-khata within Greater Bengaluru Authority limits are stuck, with portal glitches and faulty document uploads holding up their applications for more than 10 days now. Without A-khata, owners struggle to access civic services, complete property transactions or get bank loans. Many said sales and registrations had stalled, while some claimed their applications were rejected despite repeated online attempts. Thereâs no clear indication of how soon the system will be restored, sources said. The delay follows the Sept 22 launch of upgraded e-Aasthi 2.0 software, meant to simplify khata services, cut paperwork and reduce visits to govt offices. Citizens soon complained of trouble uploading documents. GBA officials said minor glitches in the early days had been fixed and maintained there were no major problems with the software, but complaints continued. Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda told TOI officials found some owners had uploaded blank files, wrong property photographs or incorrect locations. âIâve instructed officials to hold special adalats and clear pending applications soon,â he added. Then deputy CM DK Shivakumar had announced the Namma Khate Namma Hakku campaign, with a 100-day window that ended on Aug 23 and it was subsequently extended. The govt cut the conversion fee from 5% to 2% of guidance value for applications filed by that date. It has since returned to 5%. The campaign targeted 7 lakh eligible B-khata properties among 23 lakh in GBA limits. Eligible properties were those registered on or before Sept 30, 2024, with a clear tax history and no major encroachment. Despite the 60% fee rebate, only 80,400 applications had come in by the end of Aug. The first version of e-Aasthi was introduced in the erstwhile BBMP in Oct 2024. title: Restoring fighter strength, accelerating Tejas & AMCA projects, boosting triservice synergy my top priorities: New IAF chief Ashutosh Dixit
text: NEW DELHI: New Indian Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, in his first address after taking charge on Sunday, said restoring the sanctioned fighter squadron strength, accelerating indigenous programmes like Light Combat Aircraft âTejasâ and fifth-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), and strengthening tri-services synergy will be his top priorities. âTejas MklA and lI, AMCA, Indian sensors and Indian weapons are our highest priority. We will fight with Indian solutions, and we will hold them in numbers that meet our operational demands. Our responsibility is to fight and win, but most importantly it is to deter conflict through credible air power,â the 29th IAF chief, an accomplished fighter pilot with over 3,500 flying hours, said on Sunday. He said ârestoringâ the IAF's combat strength towards the âsanctioned levelâ will also be his âforemost taskâ. Watch India Signs Rs 53,866 Crore Deal For 8 Next-Generation Navy Corvettes The new chief arrived at the parade ground in an electric vehicle, in a move reflecting his push for green mobility. Dixit outlined his core focus areas under the acronym VAYU, defining his âvisionâ as vigilance and operational readiness, âaatmanirbhartaâ (self-reliance), âyuktiâ (tactical innovation), and âunityâ of effort across the tri-services. As Indiaâs combat squadrons have depleted to 29 from the sanctioned strength of 42, the IAF is desperately seeking to raise the strength of fighters. The IAF is eagerly waiting for the induction of 180 LCA MK1A aircraft, being manufactured by Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd under two contracts. While the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) and HAL are working on the LCA Mk 2 variant, the framework for developing AMCA is being finalised. The IAF is also hoping for an early deal with France on 114 Rafale jets. On the current security situation, the new IAF chief said, âOur security environment remains demanding. In addition, the character of war is being reshaped by new technologies and systems like drones, long-range precision weapons, space, cyber, Al and the electromagnetic spectrum. The air force, while transforming into the force that India will need in the next decade, must always be ready to fight and win.â Dixit also lauded his predecessor Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, saying the IAF, under his leadership, displayed what âprecise and decisiveâ air power can achieve during Operation Sindoor. âI thank him for handing over a force in a high state of readiness,â he said. âTo the fellow citizens of my motherland, please trust that your Air Force is vigilant, ready and resolute. Our commitment is clear âto remain ready, to keep transforming and to deliver whenever the nation calls,â he said.The IAF chief also underlined his priorities for the welfare of air warriors, Agniveers (Vayu), civilians, veterans, Veer Naris and their families. âTheir training, professional excellence, morale, safety, welfare and dignity will have my personal attention. â Before receiving the guard of honour, new Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit laid a wreath at the National War Memorial (NWM) to honour fallen heroes. Accompanied by family members, he sought blessings of his mother, Nirmala Dixit, and mother-in-law, Kamla Pandey, touching their feet prior to the ceremony.

However, he said in the Channel 14 interview that, âthey were locked in a conception that it was a drill, or a small thing.â Netanyahu claimed that had he been alerted, he would have ordered a stronger response before the attack unfolded. âIf they had woken me up, they knew Iâd have woken everybody and canceled Nova and put the air force on alert,â he said, referring to the Nova music festival, where hundreds of people were killed during the Hamas-led October 7 assault. title: In 2016, Texas residents began challenging developer control of their neighbourhood associations; 10 years later, the homeowners own their park, roads, ponds and guardhouse after a long legal fight
text: Representative Image (AI-generated) For years, residents of La Bota Ranch in Laredo, Texas, questioned why developers continued to control their homeownersâ associations while residents paid rising fees to maintain their community. A decade after homeowners began organising against the arrangement, the associations have taken ownership of the neighbourhoodâs common areas, including its park, streets, ponds and guardhouse. According to the Laredo Morning Timesâ October 26, 2026, report, which quotes longtime resident and Laredo City Council member Vanessa Perez, the transfer was completed on August 20, 2026, following years of litigation and settlement negotiations. The transfer followed years of disputes over rising fees, developer control and the management of the communityâs shared property. Rising fees prompted homeowners to organise La Bota Ranch is a master-planned residential community in north Laredo, developed in the early 1990s. Its two homeownersâ associations oversee different sections of the neighbourhood and fund services such as private road maintenance and the upkeep of parks and other facilities. The dispute gained momentum in 2016, when homeowners saw substantial increases in their association dues. According to a July 2017 report by Laredo Morning Times, annual fees for the La Bota Ranch Owners Association rose from $1,328 in 2015 to $2,268 in 2016. Fees for the La Bota Property Owners Association increased from $1,651 to $2,600 over the same period. Residents questioned the increases and raised concerns about declining services, spending and their lack of representation on the association boards. The developers continued to control the boards, while homeowners argued that they should have a greater say in decisions affecting their properties and shared amenities. In June 2017, five residents filed a lawsuit against developer Albert F. Muller III and other individuals associated with the developer-controlled boards. The case sought accountability and greater homeowner representation in the management of the associations. A jury sided with residents after years of litigation The dispute continued for several years as homeowners challenged the developersâ control and sought changes to the associationsâ governance. Residents also raised concerns about the boardsâ financial decisions and their fiduciary responsibilities. In March 2022, a jury ruled in favour of the homeowners. According to KGNS and Laredo Morning Times, the jury found that the defendants had breached their fiduciary duties. The dispute involved concerns about fee increases and whether the developer-controlled boards had fulfilled their responsibilities to homeowners. In July 2022, Webb County Judge Joe Lopez ordered four board members, Albert Muller III, Albert Muller Jr., Virginia Muller and Greg Ebe, to be removed from their positions and prohibited them from directly or indirectly managing, supervising, directing or approving decisions made on behalf of either association. A new homeowner board was appointed on January 19, 2023. However, the change in board membership did not immediately resolve the dispute over control of the communityâs land and common property. The associations continued working towards a settlement that would transfer ownership of the shared areas to the homeowners. Dispute over nearby development added another challenge While the governance dispute continued, residents also opposed a proposed warehouse near Muller Elementary School. Homeowners raised concerns about the compatibility of industrial development with the surrounding residential area. In 2024, Laredo adopted an ordinance restricting the parking or storage of certain large commercial vehicles near schools, parks and other specified locations, according to Perezâs account in the October 2026 report. The property owner subsequently challenged the city and Perez over the restriction. In November 2025, the city settled the dispute by purchasing the contested property. Separately, the associations filed another lawsuit against the developers in October 2024 involving governance, property ownership and related rights. Settlement agreements began in February 2026, initiating the transition towards homeowner control. Homeowners take ownership of shared property The final transfer marked a significant change for the community. On August 20, 2026, the associations completed the closing that transferred ownership of the common-area property to the homeownersâ associations. Perez, who has lived in La Bota Ranch since 2011 and was among the residents involved in the original legal fight, described the outcome as the culmination of a decade of work by homeowners, association board members and their attorneys. The property transferred includes the community centre, park, streets, soccer field, ponds, guardhouse and other common areas. The associationsâ ownership gives the homeowner-controlled bodies responsibility for these shared assets, rather than leaving them under the previous developer-controlled arrangement. For La Bota Ranch homeowners, the August 2026 transfer marked the culmination of a decade-long effort to gain greater control over their communityâs governance and shared property. What began with concerns about rising fees and representation ultimately led to years of litigation and a settlement that transferred ownership of the common areas to the homeownersâ associations. title: US midterms 2026: Early voting surpasses 50.5 million, Texas sees significant voter turnout increase
text: Over 50.5 million early votes cast by Saturday morning/Image: Reuters More than 50.5 million Americans have voted early ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections, nearly five million more than the total recorded during the 2022 midterms. The increase comes as both parties face closely contested races that could determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term. Data from the University of Florida's Election Lab showed that early voting had surpassed 50.5 million by Saturday morning, ahead of Tuesday's election. Among states that track voters' party affiliations, registered Democrats accounted for 10.7 million early ballots, compared with 7.8 million from registered Republicans. These figures reflect the political registration of voters who have cast ballots and do not indicate which candidates they have supported. Watch HUGE! Dissatisfaction with Trump's presidency and concerns about the cost of living have also become prominent issues in the campaign. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate and are seeking to retain control of the chamber. Democrats are targeting traditionally Republican-leaning states, including Texas, Alaska and Kansas, where competitive races could help them secure a majority. Texas has become a major focus of the contest, with more than seven million people having already voted early, as per the University data. This is around 1.5 million more than the number recorded in the state during the 2022 midterms. The increase is also evident in Harris County, which includes Houston. By Wednesday, 862,700 people had cast early ballots there, compared with 564,500 at the same point in the 2022 election, the Associated Press analysis has found. Harris County has consistently backed Democratic candidates in recent elections. In 2024, Kamala Harris defeated Trump in the county by nearly six percentage points in the presidential election. Democratic Senate candidate Colin Allred also won the county by roughly 11 percentage points over Republican incumbent Ted Cruz. This year's Texas Senate contest has drawn national attention, with Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton facing Democratic candidate James Talarico. Republican Governor Greg Abbott is also seeking re-election against Democrat Gina Hinojosa. Early voting has also increased in other states with competitive Senate races. In Kansas, where Republicans face another closely contested Senate race, early voting is up 34%. Maine has recorded a 44% increase, while Michigan has seen a rise of 32%, the AP reported. The midterm elections will determine the composition of the House of Representatives and Senate for the remaining two years of Trump's term. Rising prices of food, petrol and other essentials, the war involving Iran and concerns about government corruption have featured in the political debate ahead of the vote. Trump has held rallies across several states to support Republican candidates, including in areas that have traditionally been considered safe for the party. title: Dalal Street braces for volatile week
text: Geopolitical tensions and soaring crude prices are fuelling market volatility, weakening the rupee and driving foreign investors away from Indian stocks. title: Netanyahu pushing Donald Trump for nuclear strike on Iran? US commentator makes big claim
text: File photo: US President Donald Trump and Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu US media personality and political commentator Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing US President Donald Trump to launch a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Washington could take a decision on the use of nuclear weapons within days. In a detailed post on X on Monday, Carlson claimed that the proposed target could be Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Tehran has restarted its nuclear enrichment programme. He argued that conventional US weapons would not be able to penetrate the mountain's granite to reach underground tunnels where enrichment activity is supposedly taking place. "Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran," Carlson wrote. He further claimed that Netanyahu had been pushing for such an operation and quoted an unnamed source as saying, "Bibi calls Trump about it every day." Carlson's post did not provide independently verifiable evidence for the claims about a possible nuclear strike or the alleged pressure being exerted by Netanyahu. Carlson claims Netanyahu wants war to continue Carlson linked the alleged push for military action to Netanyahu's political position following last week's elections in Israel. He claimed the Israeli prime minister would struggle to form a government without Trump's direct intervention and could face investigations and possible jail if he lost office. "Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war," Carlson wrote. He also alleged that several senior US officials were backing Netanyahu's position and opposed a negotiated settlement with Iran. Carlson named US defence secretary Pete Hegseth and Centcom commander Brad Cooper, while also claiming that secretary of state Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe were following the Israeli prime minister's lead. Carlson further claimed that former US president Barack Obama had opposed the Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha during a recent meeting. He did not provide details or evidence to substantiate that assertion either. The commentator also said that Netanyahu had travelled secretly to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to seek the United Arab Emirates' support for a final military operation against Iran, but that the Emiratis had refused. Warning over regional and global consequences Carlson warned that another escalation could have serious consequences for the Gulf region and the global economy, pointing to damage to oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and disruptions to energy and fertiliser markets. He claimed that 11 of the approximately 850 supertankers used to transport oil globally had been badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October. On the consequences of a possible nuclear strike, Carlson alleged that a ground explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Persian Gulf and affect the water supply of 100 million people. He also warned that the use of a nuclear weapon by the US could set a precedent for other countries. Carlson claimed that Russia had told at least two governments that a US nuclear strike on Iran would give it the freedom to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. He also cited possible nuclear escalation involving North Korea and South Korea. He further alleged that the US administration had quietly revised its nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier. Trump weighing diplomacy as Iran talks continue Carlson's claims come amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to resume negotiations between Washington and Tehran, even as the possibility of renewed military action remains under discussion. US President Donald Trump and Netanyahu spoke by phone on Saturday about the state of negotiations with Iran and the possibility of returning to military operations, according to an Axios report. The report said Netanyahu was pressing Trump to launch fresh strikes after Tuesday's US midterm elections, while the US president wanted to allow negotiations to continue. An Israeli source described the conversation as "tough", while a US source called it "direct". Trump later described the conversation as a "very good talk" and confirmed that Iran was among the subjects discussed, without providing further details. Trump has said negotiations with Iran were "going fine" and that he was not "in much of a hurry". However, he also indicated that the US still needed to address one or two Iranian nuclear sites, specifically referring to Pickaxe Mountain. "We can do that in 10 minutes. We have that planned. You can look at Pickaxe Mountain. We need to take care of that. We can do that very quickly," Trump said. Meanwhile, US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter last week to Iran's national security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, regarding the possibility of restarting negotiations. Qatari mediators also held discussions with Iranian officials for a third consecutive day on Sunday in an effort to facilitate an agreement to resume direct talks between Washington and Tehran. Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said no agreement had been reached and that progress depended on the US responding to Tehran's questions. "We are making every effort in this regard and hope that the other side will demonstrate enough rationality to choose diplomacy over other paths," Araghchi said. title: Builder ordered to refund â¹63 lakh with interest over delayed Zirakpur flat
text: The commission, comprising presiding member Padma Pandey and member Rajesh K Arya, found the firm guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices regarding an apartment in Zirakpur Chandigarh: Bringing major relief to a homebuyer couple left waiting despite paying nearly 95% of their flatâs cost, the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, UT Chandigarh, has directed a real estate firm and its two directors to refund â¹62.7 lakh with 12% annual interest from the respective dates of deposit. The commission, comprising presiding member Padma Pandey and member Rajesh K Arya, found the firm guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices regarding an apartment in Zirakpur. The builder and its directors were also ordered to pay â¹75,000 as compensation for mental agony and â¹35,000 in litigation costs within 30 days. Complainants Saurabh Verma and his wife Puja Rani booked a 1,590-square-foot flat for â¹66.5 lakh in October 2022, with an original possession deadline of Oct 31, 2023. Despite receiving â¹62.7 lakhâincluding a â¹40.1 lakh home loanâthe developer failed to hand over the property on time. The deadline was extended three times across Sept 2023, Aug 2024, and Aug 2025, pushing the delivery target to November 2024, July 2025, and finally Dec 31, 2025. While the builder initially paid â¹30,000 per month as delayed-possession compensation for a year, the payments stopped thereafter. The commission ruled that these monthly payments received between Nov 2023 and Nov 2024 will be adjusted against the final refund. The buyers alleged the firm demanded additional funds for finishing work despite slow construction, threatening contract cancellation and 24% interest for non-payment. When the firm issued a possession letter on Sept 27, 2025, the buyers refused it, citing incomplete construction and missing statutory approvals. An RTI response dated Jan 2, 2026, confirmed the lack of a fire safety certificate. The commission observed that offering a possession letter without required statutory clearances does not make a unit fit for occupation. It noted that the firmâs defense was struck off on April 16, 2026, after it failed to file a written reply within the 45-day window. Relying on Supreme Court precedents, the commission affirmed that buyers cannot be forced to wait indefinitely or take possession of an incomplete unit. âThe obligation of a builder is not merely to construct a structure or issue a letter describing possession as offered; it is to deliver the contracted residential unit within the stipulated period, in a habitable condition and in conformity with the applicable statutory requirements,â the commission observed. It held that repeated delays, halting compensation, and demanding extra funds constituted material service deficiency under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, adding: âThe fact that the complainants have paid approximately 95% of the total sale consideration makes their predicament all the more serious, as a substantial part of their financial resources stands committed to a unit whose lawful and habitable possession has not been established. â You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in Chandigarh Stay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. title: Travis Kelce vs Patrick Mahomes: Which Chiefs superstar has made a bigger impact through charitable donations and community work?
text: Travis Kelce and Patrick mahomes(Image via Getty Images) Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have built extraordinary careers in Kansas City, winning championships and earning millions along the way. But their influence extends well beyond the football field. Both Chiefs superstars have invested heavily in charitable causes, supported children from disadvantaged backgrounds and helped strengthen their communities through their respective foundations. From Kelce's nearly $2 million contribution to Operation Breakthrough to Mahomes' multimillion-dollar grants for youth organisations, their generosity has become an important part of their legacies. While their approaches differ, their shared commitment raises an interesting question: Which Chiefs star has made a bigger impact through charity? Travis Kelce's charity work focuses on education and opportunities for underserved children Kelce's charitable journey began with a personal connection to the struggles faced by young people. Growing up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, the tight end saw how access to resources and opportunities could shape a child's future. That experience inspired him to establish the Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation in 2015. The organisation aims to help disadvantaged young people develop skills through education, business, athletics, science, technology, engineering, mathematics and the arts. Rather than limiting its work to financial assistance, Kelce's foundation focuses on giving children the tools to build independent futures. One of his most significant commitments has been his partnership with Operation Breakthrough, a Kansas City nonprofit that supports children and families experiencing poverty. Kelce has contributed nearly $2 million to the organisation over the years through personal donations and directed funds, according to the Kansas City Chiefs. His most ambitious project with the organisation is the Ignition Lab. In 2020, Kelce announced plans to purchase an old building in Kansas City and transform it into a learning and workforce development centre for teenagers. The project became a reality in 2021, providing students aged 14 to 18 with opportunities to explore careers in engineering, automotive work, coding, digital media and entrepreneurship. The centre has helped more than 1,000 students since opening. Its purpose goes beyond classroom lessons, allowing teenagers to gain practical experience and discover possible career paths before entering adulthood. Kelce has also supported his hometown through the Heights Schools Foundation. His contributions have helped more than 2,300 children access remote learning, after-school programmes, tutoring and inspirational speakers. His generosity became particularly visible following the February 2024 Kansas City parade shooting. Two young sisters from the Reyes family suffered gunshot wounds during the incident. Kelce's Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation made two separate $50,000 donations to their family's fundraiser, bringing the total contribution to $100,000. The money helped cover their medical recovery and future needs. He has continued supporting Operation Breakthrough through annual fundraising events. His Celebrity Challenge brings together athletes from Kansas City's professional sports teams to raise money for the nonprofit. In October 2026, the event returned for its seventh edition. Kelce has also won Nationwide's Charity Challenge three times. His latest victory in January 2026 secured another $35,000 donation for Operation Breakthrough. He previously earned the same award in 2020 and 2025, making him the first three-time winner of the programme. Patrick Mahomes' foundation has distributed millions to children's charities While Kelce has built a strong connection with a few major organisations, Mahomes has developed a wider charitable network through his 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Established in 2019, the foundation focuses on improving children's lives through health, education, wellness and community support. Patrick and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have backed several projects across Kansas City and Texas, with grants reaching schools, youth organisations and community programmes. One of their biggest contributions came in 2021, when the foundation donated $1 million towards the redevelopment of Martin Luther King Jr. Park in Kansas City. The funding helped create an inclusive playground where children with different physical and mental abilities could play together. The project became an important community space, with accessible equipment and features designed to welcome children of all abilities. Mahomes also attended the opening ceremony, celebrating the playground with local families. In October 2023, the foundation announced another major commitment. It pledged $1.625 million to Boys & Girls Clubs of America through a multi-year partnership. The contribution supports children in Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, Texas. The partnership also introduced an additional fundraising element. The foundation committed to donating $1,500 for every regular-season touchdown scored by Mahomes, creating another way to connect his NFL performances with youth development. His foundation has also supported food security and children's healthcare. In 2022, it distributed more than 15,000 meals through food bank partnerships and worked with OneSight Vision Clinic to provide free eye examinations and glasses to more than 100 children in the Kansas City area. Mahomes has also supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, granting wishes to 10 children with serious illnesses. His involvement included spending time with young fans and helping create memorable experiences for their families. Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce support different causes through their foundations Their charitable work shares a common goal, but the way they approach it reveals two different priorities. Kelce has built much of his philanthropic identity around long-term involvement. His relationship with Operation Breakthrough goes beyond writing cheques. He regularly visits the organisation, spends time with students and helps create programmes that can support children as they grow older. His foundation also supports educational opportunities in Cleveland Heights and Kansas City. The University of Cincinnati has benefited from his support through a health and wellness endowment for student-athletes. Mahomes, meanwhile, has developed a grant-based approach that reaches a wider network of organisations. His foundation has supported groups such as Lead to Read, City Year, United Way of Greater Kansas City, Children's Mercy Hospital, Special Olympics Missouri and Kansas City Public Library. The foundation's 2024 financial records provide an idea of its reach. According to nonprofit financial data, 15 and the Mahomies distributed approximately $4.6 million through 119 grants between 2020 and 2024. Its 2024 grants included $650,000 for Boys & Girls Clubs of America, $57,500 for City Year, $50,500 for Lead to Read and $50,000 for United Way of Greater Kansas City. Mahomes has also encouraged young people to become active in their communities through programmes such as Read for 15 and Volunteer for 15. These initiatives encourage children to spend time reading and helping others rather than focusing only on receiving financial assistance. The foundation has supported scholarship programmes, food assistance and inclusive sports opportunities as well. Its work with Special Olympics Missouri and other youth organisations reflects a broader effort to reach children with different needs. Who has made a bigger charitable impact, Travis Kelce or Patrick Mahomes? Comparing the two Chiefs stars through a single donation figure would miss much of the story. Their foundations operate differently, and their financial records cover different periods. Kelce has contributed nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough alone, while his work with Ignition Lab has created lasting educational and career opportunities for teenagers. His $100,000 contribution to the Reyes family and repeated fundraising victories also demonstrate his willingness to support families facing difficult circumstances. Kelce has developed a close connection with young people through education and career development, while Mahomes has used his foundation to support a wider range of organisations. title: Biology remains top choice in UP Board, maths sees steady decline
text: Prayagraj : Biology continues to dominate the choice of UP Board intermediate students, with nearly three times as many candidates opting for the subject as for mathematics for the 2027 examinations. Registration data show that 11,63,401 students have selected biology, compared with 3,99,965 who have chosen mathematics. The figures are part of the registration data for 24,38,883 students appearing for the intermediate examinations in 2027. Of these, 15,63,366 students are from the science stream, making biology the largest single subject choice among them. Education experts said the preference for biology is linked to the broader range of career options available to students after intermediate. âBesides MBBS, students can pursue courses in Ayurveda, homeopathy, dentistry and veterinary sciences. Paramedical programmes, healthcare, agriculture, animal husbandry and basic sciences also offer career pathways,â said Anglo Bengali Inter College principal Swastik Bose. UP Board secretary Bhagwati Singh said the wider career opportunities in biology and apprehension about mathematics among students could be contributing to the difference in enrolment. The figures also indicate that the preference is not a recent development. Biology enrolment has remained above the 10-lakh mark during the past five years. It stood at 10,84,932 in 2023 before rising to 11,34,114 in 2024 and 12,49,460 in 2025. The figure was 12,16,270 in 2026 and stood at 11,63,401 for 2027. Mathematics, meanwhile, has witnessed a steady decline over the same period. The number of students opting for the subject fell from 4,99,484 in 2023 to 4,50,097 in 2024, 4,25,257 in 2025 and 3,98,567 in 2026, before marginally rising to 3,99,965 in 2027. Among humanities subjects, sociology is the most popular, with 4,22,590 registrations, followed by political science at 3,60,344 and geography at 3,17,036. title: $8,000 monthly fuel bills force US luxury cruise to halt world voyage, leaving 200 stranded
text: The ship was carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, and 156 crew members Imagine selling your house, giving up life on land and spending hundreds of thousands of dollars to make a luxury cruise ship your permanent home, only to be told to disembark thousands of miles away from home because the voyage can no longer afford to keep sailing. That is the reality facing more than 200 passengers aboard the MV Odyssey, a residential cruise ship whose ambitious round-the-world journey has been suspended in Cambodia amid soaring fuel costs. The vessel, which set sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland, in October 2024 for a journey spanning all seven continents and more than 400 destinations, arrived at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville last Friday. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, subsequently announced that mounting operating expenses had made continuing the voyage financially unsustainable, leaving passengers scrambling to arrange accommodation and alternative travel. According to Cambodian officials, the ship was carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, and 156 crew members. The company said it was coordinating disembarkation and temporary living arrangements while exploring restructuring and recapitalisation options over the next 60 days. The vessel's future, however, remains uncertain. Iran war pushes fuel bills beyond sustainable levels The suspension comes amid a surge in global oil prices linked to the war involving Iran, which has disrupted fuel supplies and curtailed traffic through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. The resulting pressure on petroleum-based fuel supplies has been particularly acute in parts of Southeast Asia. Villa Vie Residences said monthly fuel expenses per cabin, which had historically averaged around $1,800, had climbed to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia. The company said it had attempted to limit the impact by reducing fuel consumption, slowing the ship's itinerary and spending more time in port. However, these measures failed to offset the increase in operating costs. âWe have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses,â the company said in a statement, adding that passing the entire increase on to residents was not a realistic solution. The operator said it was coordinating disembarkation and temporary living arrangements while considering ways to restructure the business. However, it cautioned that no outcome was assured. NBC News reported that passengers were given only a few hours' notice to leave the vessel, leaving some to arrange their own accommodation and travel. Cambodian officials said some passengers had already flown out, while others remained in Sihanoukville. The ship was expected to refuel before leaving Cambodia on Saturday, according to the province's deputy governor, Long Dimanche. However, the operator had not publicly confirmed a departure date. Passengers allege mismanagement as dream voyage stalls The financial pressures have also revived concerns among residents about the company's management and the sustainability of its residential cruising model. The Odyssey was marketed as a floating home, offering passengers the opportunity to combine long-term living at sea with global travel. The company advertised lifetime cabin ownership, with prices for some berths starting at around $230,000, alongside rental options. However, some residents told the Associated Press that the company had faced financial difficulties even before the latest fuel price surge. Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming who boarded the ship 17 months ago, said changes to the itinerary, unreliable internet access and declining food quality had prompted some residents to leave. Lynn Montoya said passengers had repeatedly been asked to contribute additional money for fuel and other expenses. She also alleged that crew members had not been paid. âWe were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything,â she said, blaming what she described as mismanagement for the venture's difficulties. Others remain hopeful that the voyage can be revived. Carol Larson, 69, who spent 18 months aboard the ship with her sister, said she hoped residents might be able to buy the vessel and continue living at sea. âBecause it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk,â Larson told the AP, adding that she did not regret taking part in the experiment. The Odyssey, built in 1993 and acquired by Villa Vie Residences in 2023, began its current voyage in October 2024 after being refitted in Belfast. title: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia takes charge as IAF vice chief
text: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia takes charge as the Indian Air Force's Vice Chief of the Air Staff, succeeding Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit. NEW DELHI: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia on Sunday assumed the appointment of Vice Chief of the Air Staff (VCAS) of the Indian Air Force . He took over from Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who now has assumed charge as 29th IAF chief. On Sunday, he paid homage at the National War Memorial and was presented a ceremonial Guard of Honour. He was earlier Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Eastern Air Command. In a career spanning almost four decades, the Air Officer has tenanted various command and staff appointments. He has commanded a frontline fighter squadron, the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment (TACDE) and was Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Bareilly. He is qualified on all variants of MiG-21, MiG-23, MiG-27, Jaguar and Su-30 MKI. Watch India Signs Rs 53,866 Crore Deal For 8 Next-Generation Navy Corvettes He had undergone Advanced Command & Staff Course in the UK and NDC in Bangladesh, headed Directorate of Air Staff Inspection (DASI) of the IAF, served as a defence attache at the Embassy of Japan and South Korea, and was the Senior Air Staff Officer of Eastern Air Command. Walia is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and was commissioned in the fighter stream of the IAF on June 11, 1988. He is an avid reader and holds three postgraduate degrees in Defence and Strategic Studies. In recognition of distinguished service, he was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal (VM) in 2008 and Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM) in 2018.

title: India's RE policies a role model for emerging economies: Analysis
text: India is actively seeking to attract $220 billion in investments to expand its renewable energy sector. NEW DELHI: As India looks to attract international investment and deepen cooperation in clean energy, green hydrogen, storage and manufacturing at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE), a new international analysis has described the country as a ârole modelâ in developing its renewable power sector, crediting its policy and regulatory measures for addressing investment risks and creating an environment conducive to private capital. The assessment comes at a time when India is looking to mobilise around $220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030 to expand renewable energy capacity, manufacturing, transmission infrastructure and energy storage as it works towards its target of 500 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Govt has already secured $64 billion in private investment between June 2024 and June 2026, including $6.2 billion in foreign direct investment, MNRE secretary Santosh Sarangi told reporters earlier this week. The recent analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics, titled Emerging market financing for renewables , said India had adopted a holistic approach to addressing risks related to project development, construction and market access, describing the country as âa renewables powerhouse built on enabling policiesâ. The report said India's long-term target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, backed by an annual bidding trajectory of 50 GW of renewable energy capacity through FY28, provides visibility to developers and investors. It also highlighted govtâs decision to allow up to 100% foreign direct investment in the electricity sector. Among the measures aimed at reducing project development risks, the analysis cited the Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Power Parks scheme, which provides developers access to land and transmission infrastructure, along with capital and interest subsidies for renewable energy projects. It also pointed to viability gap funding for offshore wind projects, including support for the development of India's first offshore wind farms. On the demand side, the report said renewable consumption obligations, which require distribution companies and large industrial and commercial consumers to source a specified proportion of their electricity from renewable sources, have helped create an expanding market for green power. Access to day-ahead and intra-day power exchanges has also widened avenues for generators to sell electricity. The analysis also highlighted measures introduced by govt in 2022 to address delays in payments by distribution companies to power generators, which had been a major concern for renewable energy developers. Outstanding dues of distribution companies, which stood at Rs 1.4 lakh crore in 2022, declined to Rs 4,109 crore in Feb 2026, it said. The report estimated that capital expenditure on solar and onshore wind projects across emerging and developing economies could reach $356 billion by 2040 if current trends continue. A senior industry executive said Indiaâs policies to boost investment in the renewable energy sector over the past two decades had catalysed green energy growth and helped the country meet its Paris Agreement goals ahead of schedule. âFurther investment focus is now required in the countryâs solar supply chain. India will continue to lead in renewable energy growth and investment attractiveness, thanks to the conducive policy environment and resilience of the Indian solar industry,â the executive said. title: A Virginia textile mill built in 1920 closed in 1996 and stood largely empty for decades; after a $110 million redevelopment, it now has residents and offices, with 190 apartments planned across the complex
text: The 1920-built White Mill in Danville, Virginia, operated for 75 years before closing in 1996. Renamed Dan River Falls, the 650,000-square-foot historic complex is being transformed into apartments, offices, retail space and a riverfront community hub. A historic textile mill in Danville, Virginia, that once symbolised the cityâs industrial prosperity has found a new purpose as a residential and commercial complex after decades of disuse. According to developer The Alexander Company, the former White Mill, built in 1920 and operated as Mill No. 8, is being redeveloped into Dan River Falls, a project valued at $110 million that combines 190 apartments with office space and retail facilities. The developer says the first residents moved in after the initial phase was completed in November 2024, while the redevelopment is scheduled for completion in 2026. The transformation reflects a broader effort to preserve Danvilleâs industrial heritage while bringing underused historic buildings back into economic and community life. The reinforced-concrete structure, which occupies more than 18 acres along the Dan River, is among the last surviving reminders of the cityâs once-powerful textile manufacturing industry. Rather than demolishing the ageing mill, the redevelopment aims to retain its historic character while adapting its interiors for modern residential and commercial use. From textile production to a vacant industrial landmark White Mill was built by Dan River Inc. in 1920 and began operating in 1921. Designed by Lockwood, Greene & Company, the five-storey building featured a simplified Gothic Revival architectural style and a distinctive reinforced-concrete structure. Its scale reflected the importance of textile manufacturing to Danville, where mills provided employment for generations of local families. The mill operated until 1996. As the textile industry declined, the building eventually stood largely idle, becoming a physical reminder of the economic changes that had reshaped the region. The decline of the wider textile industry cost Danville thousands of jobs, leaving former industrial properties struggling to find new uses. For decades, the White Mill remained a prominent feature along the riverfront, with the words âHome of Dan River Fabricsâ once welcoming visitors arriving in the city. Its deteriorating condition presented a challenge: how could a vast industrial building be preserved without leaving it as an unused relic of the past? The answer came through a partnership between The Alexander Company, a Wisconsin-based historic redevelopment specialist, and the Danville Industrial Development Authority. A $110 million effort to preserve history The redevelopment effort began taking shape after years of discussions about how to reuse the property. In May 2021, Danville officials announced a partnership between the cityâs Industrial Development Authority and The Alexander Company to convert White Mill into a mixed-use development. The original proposal called for 150 apartments and 110,000 square feet of commercial space in the first phase, with another 100 apartments planned for a later phase. Rehabilitation work began in December 2022. The project was subsequently named Dan River Falls, and the first phase was completed in November 2024. The developer's current plans list 190 apartments, 147,000 square feet of office space and a project completion date of 2026. The total investment is reported at approximately $110 million. According to Virginia Business, the redevelopment involved a public-private partnership in which The Alexander Company led the residential component, while the city and its partners oversaw commercial and public-facing elements. State and federal historic tax credits, alongside other financing arrangements, helped support the undertaking. Residents, offices and a new riverfront destination The apartments are not the only sign of the building's return to use. By October 2025, 150 apartments in the first phase had become home to more than 275 people, and another 40 units were being made available. The developer also says the housing includes options for workers earning less than 80% of the area's median income, linking the project to local workforce housing needs. The former mill is also accommodating public offices and private businesses. In early 2026, Danville's Office of Economic Development and Tourism moved into the complex, joining the city's Parks and Recreation department. Engineering and consulting firm Dewberry also relocated its Danville office to the property. The project extends beyond the mill's walls. Plans include a riverfront park, an extension of the city's Riverwalk Trail and space for retail and other commercial activities. The developer's website describes more than seven acres of riverfront parkland as part of the wider development vision. Preserving the original structure while adapting it for new uses has been central to the project. The work retains the building's reinforced-concrete framework and historic architectural character while creating interiors suited to modern living and working. The redevelopment was also recognised by Virginia Business as one of the state's notable projects in 2026, reflecting the scale of the conversion and the partnership behind it. title: 'No excuse for victim blaming': Mamdani under fire from Democrats and pro-Palestinian left over Oct 7 message
text: File photo: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani attends a vigil marking the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks on Israel Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani âs statement marking the third anniversary of Hamasâ October 7 attack on Israel has drawn criticism from both sides of the US political divide. Democrats and Jewish groups accusing him of shifting attention from the victims of the attack to Israelâs war in Gaza, while some on the pro-Palestinian left say he did not go far enough. Mamdaniâs statement began by calling October 7, 2023, a âprofoundly painfulâ day and condemning Hamasâ âhorrific war crimesâ, including the killing of about 1,200 people in Israel and the taking of more than 250 hostages. âWe grieve alongside our many friends and neighbors who still carry that unthinkable loss,â he said. But Mamdani then turned to Israelâs military campaign in Gaza, calling it a âdevastating, ongoing genocideâ and citing more than 74,000 deaths recorded by the Hamas-controlled Gaza health ministry. âMany New Yorkers are reckoning with this unbearable grief, and we mourn alongside them â all while knowing that our tax dollars fund these war crimes,â Mamdani said. He added that three years later, âoccupation and apartheid continueâ, while accusing the US federal government of complicity through arms shipments. The statement drew fierce criticism from several Democratic lawmakers, who said Mamdani had made the anniversary about Israel rather than Hamas and the people killed and abducted on October 7. Florida representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz accused Mamdani of âdesecrating the memory of murdered, innocent Jewsâ, while New Jersey representative Josh Gottheimer said the mayor was âblaming the victimsâ. Jersey City mayor Steven Fulop called the statement âinappropriate and unnecessarily inflammatoryâ. New York representative Dan Goldman called the message âegregious and insultingâ. Goldman told Politico that October 7 should be reserved for remembering what he described as a horrific terror attack, rather than using the occasion to focus on the broader conflict. âRegardless of what you actually think of the conflict and whatâs happened either since or before, thereâs no excuse for victim blaming,â Goldman said. Brad Lander, the Mamdani-backed Democrat who defeated Goldman in this yearâs primary, took a more nuanced position. He condemned Hamas but argued against forcing people to choose between mourning the victims of October 7 and acknowledging Palestinian suffering. âWe can mourn for those lost on October 7th and still acknowledge the enormous imbalance of power between Israel and the Palestinians,â Lander wrote. Mamdani also faced criticism from Jewish organisations. Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt said the mayorâs statement did not mention Jews and accused him of using a day meant for mourning the victims of the attack to repeat his anti-Zionist arguments. US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called the statement an âoutrageous & disgusting rantâ, while Ofir Akunis, Israelâs consul general in New York, called it a âdisgrace, shame, and insult to the memory of those who were murderedâ. About 200 anti-Israel protesters gathered outside City Hall on Wednesday evening, with some accusing Mamdani of betraying the Palestinian cause. Several protesters told Politico they had voted for Mamdani but would not support him for re-election because they were unhappy that he had not fired NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch, whom they described as a Zionist, or stopped some New York synagogues from hosting events promoting land sales in the occupied West Bank. The protestersâ criticism reflected a broader frustration among some activists that Mamdani, despite his longstanding opposition to Israelâs policies, had not gone far enough in confronting Israel or supporting the Palestinian cause. At the same time, senator Bernie Sanders, an independent who is a close adviser to Mamdani, defended the mayorâs basic framing of the conflict. Sanders said Israel had the right to defend itself and target Hamas after the October 7 attack, but accused Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahuâs government of waging âa genocide against the Palestinian people in Gazaâ. His strong criticism of Israel helped energise young and progressive voters during his mayoral campaign, while also making him a frequent target of Jewish groups, Israeli officials and more moderate Democrats. title: Chintels Paradiso Tower J declared unsafe in Gurgaon, set to be demolished in 3 months; until demolition, developer must barricade and fence site, display danger signs
text: Gurgaon: MCG has declared Tower-J of Chintels Paradiso in Sector 109 a dangerous building and directed its developer, Chintels India, to demolish the structure within three months, subject to statutory approvals and Supreme Court directions. Towers D, E, F, G and H have already been demolished after being declared unsafe. The order, issued by MCG commissioner Pradeep Dahiya under Section 265(2) of Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1994, says the tower is structurally unsafe and likely to endanger people occupying, visiting or passing near it. The order relies on an IIT Delhi structural assessment, which found significant distress in the building, deterioration of reinforced concrete members, excessive chloride contamination, corrosion of reinforcement steel and loss of structural durability. The institute concluded that Tower-J was unsafe for continued occupation. The order takes effect immediately and does not replace other statutory permissions. Until demolition, the developer must barricade and fence the site, display danger signs, prevent unauthorised entry and deploy round-the-clock security. It must protect adjoining buildings, roads and public places during the work. Before demolition, the company must obtain MCG approval for a construction and demolition waste management plan, register on the civic bodyâs C&D waste portal and comply with the 2025 waste management rules, CAQM directions and dust-control measures. Debris must be transported only to authorised facilities. If the developer fails to comply, MCG can take steps to remove the danger, including demolishing the structure, and recover the expenses from the company as arrears of municipal tax. The developer must carry out demolition through a competent agency at its own cost and responsibility. The three-month period will include compliance with restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). Any extension can be granted only by the commissioner. The order refers to the Supreme Courtâs order dated Sept 3, 2026 and records the courtâs direction that unsafe towers be vacated by Jan 1, 2027 and redevelopment commence on or before March 31, 2027. The action follows the structural failure in Tower-D of the project on Feb 10, 2022, which caused loss of life and raised concerns about the safety of other towers. A committee constituted by the district administration also found the tower unsafe for habitation and recommended permanent closure and demolition, saying repair and rehabilitation were not technically viable. The order cites the collapse of a portion of a balcony in Tower-J on Jan 12, 2024, as further evidence of the continuing risk. Chintels India had submitted a representation on Sept 29, seeking permission to demolish Tower-J through its appointed agency, Edifice Engineering. MCG has directed the company to begin demolition immediately after lawful vacation and completion of statutory pre-demolition requirements.
