title: After directing Schindlerâs List in 1993, Steven Spielberg donated his share of the filmâs profits to a foundation; the organisation has since distributed more than $160 million in grants
text: When Steven Spielberg directed Schindlerâs List in 1993, the experience left a lasting impact on him, inspiring a philanthropic commitment that has continued for decades. The filmmaker donated his share of the filmâs profits to establish the Righteous Persons Foundation in 1994, with the aim of strengthening Jewish life, preserving historical memory and supporting initiatives that promote social justice. Since its establishment, the foundation has expanded its work beyond Holocaust education to include arts, culture, documentary filmmaking and efforts to build understanding between communities. According to its official website, the organisation has distributed more than $160 million in grants, supporting projects that preserve Jewish heritage, amplify overlooked stories and encourage a more inclusive society. How Schindlerâs List inspired the foundation Released in 1993, Schindlerâs List tells the story of German industrialist Oskar Schindler, who saved more than 1,000 Jews during the Holocaust by employing them in his factories. The film, based on Thomas Keneallyâs novel Schindlerâs Ark, brought the history of the Holocaust to a global audience and became one of Spielbergâs most acclaimed works. Spielbergâs experience directing the film motivated him to establish the Righteous Persons Foundation the following year. In August 1994, the Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that all his personal profits from the film would go towards the newly established organisation. The foundation began operating in the autumn of 1994, with its initial priorities including Holocaust education and support for Jewish causes in the United States. The foundationâs vision was not limited to preserving the past. It also sought to strengthen contemporary Jewish communities by supporting education, cultural initiatives and social justice efforts. A philanthropic effort that grew beyond one film The foundationâs work expanded as Spielberg and his wife, actress Kate Capshaw, contributed additional funds. Spielberg also designated profits from his films Munich (2005) and Lincoln (2012) for the organisation, according to its official website. In 2005, profits from Munich, which explores the aftermath of the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre, helped establish the foundationâs Media Fund for Co-existence. An initial $5 million allocation supported projects using media and storytelling to encourage understanding between people from different backgrounds. Among the initiatives supported through the fund were Arab Labor, a television sitcom about the life of an Arab Israeli journalist, and Israel Story, a radio programme and podcast exploring Israeli society. The projects reflected the foundationâs belief that storytelling can help audiences understand experiences beyond their own. More than $160 million distributed in grants The Righteous Persons Foundation reports that it has distributed more than $160 million in grants since its establishment. Its funding has supported organisations working in Jewish history, education, arts and culture, documentary filmmaking, social justice and intercultural understanding. The grants have backed both established institutions and projects seeking new ways to engage audiences with history and contemporary social issues. The foundation has also supported efforts to make Jewish cultural traditions accessible to younger generations and to encourage dialogue across religious and cultural divides. Its grantmaking has evolved over time, but its central aim remains to strengthen Jewish life while promoting dignity, justice and a deeper understanding of different communities. The $160 million figure represents the foundationâs cumulative grantmaking as reported on its own website. Preserving Holocaust survivorsâ testimonies One of the foundationâs significant areas of support has been the preservation of Holocaust survivor testimony through the USC Shoah Foundation, an independent institute established by Spielberg in 1994. The institute records and preserves the experiences of Holocaust survivors and other witnesses of genocide, making their accounts available for education and research. The Righteous Persons Foundation provided substantial support towards establishing the organisation and has continued to fund its work. In 2024, the foundation pledged $30 million over six years to the USC Shoah Foundationâs endowment. According to the grant announcement, the funding is intended to help preserve testimonies, provide opportunities for additional survivors and liberators to record their experiences, and strengthen the instituteâs educational programmes. The grant reflects a long-term commitment to ensuring that survivor accounts remain accessible to future generations, particularly as the number of living Holocaust survivors declines. The two organisations remain independent, with the USC Shoah Foundation focused on testimony and education and the Righteous Persons Foundation operating as a grantmaking organisation. Supporting documentary films and Jewish culture The foundation has also invested in documentary filmmaking as a way to explore Jewish identity, history and social issues. In 1996, it helped establish a documentary film fund at the Foundation for Jewish Culture. The fund supported projects including Trembling Before G-d, which examines the experiences of gay and lesbian Orthodox Jews, and Waltz with Bashir, an animated documentary about memory and the Lebanon War. The foundation says the initiative backed close to 100 documentaries. Another major cultural project involved the digitisation of Yiddish literature. In 1998, the foundation became the lead funder of the Yiddish Book Centerâs effort to preserve and make Yiddish books available online. The resulting Steven Spielberg Digital Yiddish Library contains digitised copies of more than 11,000 distinct titles, according to the foundation. Subsequent support helped fund translators working to make Yiddish literature available in English, widening access to a literary tradition that might otherwise be difficult for new generations to explore. Helping Holocaust survivors access reparations The foundationâs work has also included practical assistance for Holocaust survivors. In 2008, it supported Bet Tzedek, a legal services organisation, in establishing the Holocaust Survivor Justice Network. The network brought together attorneys who volunteered to help survivors navigate the process of seeking reparations from the German government. According to the foundationâs account, the network had helped more than 5,000 survivors obtain an estimated $25 million in reparations by the time of its published update. The initiative demonstrated how grantmaking could help survivors access compensation through legal assistance, particularly when complex procedures created barriers. It also extended the foundationâs work beyond historical preservation and education to address the needs of people who lived through the Holocaust. A lasting commitment to history and community The Righteous Persons Foundationâs work has developed into a broad philanthropic programme connecting cultural preservation, education, storytelling and social justice. title: Seniors left on hold: Elderly helpline goes silent in Chandigarh
text: While official records state operations halted on June 24, 2025, call logs indicate a much earlier collapse. The line received 5,088 calls in 2022â23, which dropped to 2,600 in 2023â24. Zero calls were recorded for 2024â25. Chandigarh: Chandigarhâs helpline for senior citizens, âElder Line 14567â, has been non-functional since June 2025 due to a lack of central funding, leaving elderly residents without critical support, legal guidance, or emergency rescue services. According to RTI data obtained by advocate Rajavikrant Sharma from the Chandigarh Child and Women Development Corporation Limited, central funds for the scheme have dried up. Sharma has sent representations to the Chandigarh Administration and the Union ministry of social justice and empowerment, seeking the helplineâs immediate restoration or an interim alternative. While official records state operations halted on June 24, 2025, call logs indicate a much earlier collapse. The line received 5,088 calls in 2022â23, which dropped to 2,600 in 2023â24. Zero calls were recorded for 2024â25. Similarly, field interventions plummeted from 49 in 2022â23 to nine in 2023â24, falling to zero in 2024â25. Total registered grievances also sank from 744 in 2022â23 to just 48 in 2023â24, with no complaints logged thereafter. âThis is indicative of the fact that the helpline has been non-operational since Dec 2023. The fact that 295 calls were received in Oct 2023, followed by no calls in and from Dec 2023, indicates that the helpline stopped working then,â Sharma said. Local advocacy groups have voiced strong outrage over the administrative lapse. âFor a small UT like Chandigarh, which is crowded with bureaucrats, it has failed to listen to its considerable population of senior citizens,â said RK Garg, 71, president of the Second Innings Association. âMy organisation and I have been meeting officials for about two years now. The administration has failed to raise this issue with the central government if there is a non-receipt of funds from the Centre as the RTI mentions. Our question is that if the Indian government has made a special helpline for elders, why is it not functional in the UT? It is the duty of the officials, and they have failed us. We are feeling discouraged,â Garg added. UT officials were unavailable for comment at the time of filing the report. Launched in Chandigarh on Feb 4, 2022, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana, the nationwide 14567 service covers four primary pillars: eldercare info, legal/pension advice, emotional support, and field rescues for homeless seniors. title: Chinaâs 'eyes in the sky' multiply, Indiaâs surveillance fleet faces a numbers game
text: Three of China's new KJ-3000 airborne early warning and control . (Image credit: Vantor) New satellite imagery shows four of China's KJ-3000 Airborne Early Warning and Control (AEW&C) aircraft at the Xi'an Aircraft Company factory at Xi'an-Yanliang, raising the possibility that the type is moving into serial production. The imagery, captured on October 5 and provided by Vantor, shows three KJ-3000s near the factory and a fourth at the nearby China Flight Test Establishment, US based think tank Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies assesses that four aircraft point to serial production. The KJ-3000, also called the KJ-20, is based on the four-engine Y-20B transport with Chinese-made engines. It has a large circular radome above the rear fuselage and an aerial refuelling probe above the cockpit. The first poor-quality photographs appeared in December 2024, and clearer images followed in May 2025. It is meant to address limits in China's existing large AEW&C fleet, since only four KJ-2000 aircraft, built on the Russian Il-76MD, have been completed. The Pentagon's 2025 report on China's military noted the KJ-3000's initial flight. The Chinese armed forces currently operate over around 70 AEW&C aircraft split between the air force and the navy. The most numerous of these is the smaller KJ-500 aircraft. The KJ-500 is based on the Y-9 transport aircraft, which is based on the Soviet An-12. India's own airborne early warning fleet is far smaller. The Israeli Phalcon system on Russian-built Il-76 aircraft came first, under a 2004 agreement with Israel and Russia for three systems. The first aircraft entered service in 2009, with the other two following over the next two years. Its rotating radome gives 360-degree coverage, but three aircraft cannot provide continuous cover across the northern and western airspace. The indigenous Netra Mk I was developed by DRDO's Centre for Airborne Systems on the Brazilian Embraer EMB-145. Its indigenous AESA radar in a dorsal radome gives about 240-degree coverage. The first aircraft flew with its surveillance equipment in 2011, and the IAF received its first Netra in 2017, a second in 2019 and a third in 2023. On June 25, 2026, DRDO handed over the Final Operational Clearance certificate, after the integration of additional electronic-support measures and radar-warning receivers. These aircraft were used during the Balakot airstrikes and Operation Sindoor. As of October 2026, the IAF has three Phalcon and three Netra Mk I aircraft. The air force has an estimated requirement of at least 18 such platforms. The next step is the Netra Mk II, built around six Airbus A321 aircraft acquired from Air India. In July 2026, DRDO's Centre for Airborne Systems (CABS) signed a contract with AI Engineering Services Limited to prepare the aircraft for conversion to military configuration, and a separate contract named Adani Defence Systems and Technologies as development-cum-production partner for the mission systems. Airbus Defence and Space is to deliver the modified aircraft, after which the Indian team will integrate and test the equipment. Separately, in January 2026 the IAF issued a request for information for six more AEW&C aircraft, with at least 10 hours' endurance or air refuelling, high-altitude operation and 360-degree radar coverage.

title: 3 years after Oct 7, Israel honours officer whose Hamas attack warning was ignored
text: Senior IDF officers are seen at a military conference at the Glilot Base, October 4, 2026. (Israel Defense Forces) Israel has honoured an intelligence officer who warned of an impending Hamas invasion before the October 7, 2023 attack, three years after the deadly assault exposed major failures in the countryâs military and intelligence apparatus. According to a report by The Times of Israel, IDF Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir honoured the Unit 8200 intelligence officer, identified only as Chief Warrant Officer âVavâ, during a conference at the Glilot military base examining the lessons of the October 7 disaster. The officer had warned senior commanders before the attack that Hamas was preparing to invade Israel, but her concerns were not acted upon. The officer, a member of the IDFâs elite Unit 8200 intelligence branch, had raised concerns about Hamasâs preparations for a large-scale assault in the months before October 7. According to The Times of Israel, she sent an email to several officers warning that âthe sword is comingâ and urged them to take the threat seriously. Her warning came after a September 19, 2023 Unit 8200 dossier that reportedly assessed that Hamas was training for a large-scale invasion of Israel. Despite the intelligence, the assessment did not lead to preparations that could have prevented or mitigated the attack. Zamir said the IDF must ensure that critical voices are heard and that commanders do not suppress warnings that challenge prevailing assessments. âIn our organizational culture, we must not allow a culture of pleasing, intellectual tyranny, or suppression of critical thinking,â he said. What happened on October 7 The October 7, 2023 attack began when Hamas-led militants launched a coordinated assault from the Gaza Strip into southern Israel. Fighters breached the heavily fortified Gaza border, attacked Israeli military positions and communities, and took hostages back into Gaza. According to Israeli figures, around 1,200 people were killed in the attack, most of them civilians, while around 250 people were taken hostage. The assault became the deadliest attack in Israelâs history and marked the beginning of the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. Israel responded by launching a large-scale military campaign in the Gaza Strip with the stated objective of dismantling Hamas and securing the release of the hostages. The ensuing war has resulted in extensive destruction and a major humanitarian crisis in Gaza. The attack also triggered intense scrutiny of Israelâs military and intelligence establishment, particularly over how Hamas was able to breach the border and carry out such a large-scale assault despite Israelâs extensive intelligence and surveillance capabilities. title: Civic polls to test NDAâs popularity, YSRCPâs revival bid in Visakhapatnam
text: The election is being closely watched as results in a politically neutral city such as Vizag are often seen as an indication of public mood. Pic: SS Vijay Babu Visakhapatnam : The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) election on Su nda y, Nov 1, is set to witness a keen contest between the NDA and YSRCP. The mayor seat has been allocated to the TDP as part of the seat-sharing arrangement among the TDP, BJP and Jana Sena . The election is being closely watched as results in a politically neutral city such as Vizag are often seen as an indication of public mood. The verdict is expected to offer insights into perceptions of the TDP-led govtâs performance, which will complete two and a half years in Dec, and oppositionâs role. With a sizeable, educated and politically aware electorate, the city is also expected to send a message on governance and civic issues. While the outcome in individual wards has attracted limited attention, the main focus is on the two mayoral candidates and the message voters may deliver through their mandate. The TDP is looking to continue its winning streak from the 2024 elections, when it secured a nearly five lakh majority in the Vizag MP constituency. The YSRCP, meanwhile, is equally determined to win the mayorâs post. The TDP has fielded first-time corporator Mukka Sravani, while the YSRCP has nominated senior politician and MLC Varudu Kalyani. The election has also become a prestige battle for the MLAs, as most corporator candidates are their loyalists. The MLAs played a key role in securing tickets for their supporters, making the civic polls a test of their political influence. The ticket distribution has also led to rebel candidates entering the fray, including those who have worked in their respective wards for years or had high hopes of securing party nominations. The seat-sharing arrangement among NDA partners has not gone down well with a section of their cadre. With the TDP winning all assembly seats and the two Lok Sabha constituencies partly falling under GVMC limits in 2024, local MLAs and MPs have campaigned aggressively in their respective areas. The YSRCP, which faced relatively fewer internal disputes over seat allocation, focused on reaching out to voters. Its mayoral candidate, Varudu Kalyani, a seasoned politician, actively campaigned across the city. Though 15 candidates are in the race for the mayorâs post, the main contest is between the TDP and YSRCP. The two parties have also adopted contrasting approaches in their manifestos. The NDA has focused on infrastructure development and improved civic services, while the YSRCP has centred its campaign on the âSave Vizagâ theme and pollution- and environment-related concerns. The NDA has listed nine commitments, including better drinking water supply, underground drainage, roads and street lighting. The YSRCP pledged to address drinking water shortages by improving reservoirs and ensuring a regular supply. It also promised to revive 12 proposed flyover projects, improve roads and drainage, upgrade 42 urban health centres and introduce a grievance redressal app. YSRCP mayoral candidate Varudu Kalyani said the party would protect the cityâs natural resources, environment, public assets and heritage, while ensuring that residents are not burdened with additional taxes. âWe will develop Vizag to place it among the top cities in the country. The TDP has failed to fulfil its promises even after 30 months in power,â she said. TDP mayoral candidate Mukka Sravani said a mandate for the alliance would accelerate development and improve civic services in Vizag. âIf elected, I will consider the position an opportunity to serve the people and take the city forward on all fronts,â said the former corporator. GFX Polling will be held from 7 am to 5 pm on Sunday, Nov 1 A total of 18,37,901 voters will exercise their franchise. 1,990 polling stations established across GVMC limits. 14,334 polling personnel deployed for election duties. 15 candidates in the fray for the mayorâs post. Main contest between the NDA and YSRCP. 573 candidates contesting for 120 corporator positions. Election material distribution centres established in all 10 zones. Gajuwaka has the highest number of polling stations at 329. 82 returning officers and assistant returning officers appointed for election duties. title: Raj seeks timely release of Rs 3,000cr under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
text: V Srinivas Jaipur: Rajasthan has sought the Centreâs intervention to ensure the timely release of Rs 3,000 crore under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0. Chief Secretary V Srinivas raised the issue during a meeting with Union drinking water and sanitation secretary Ashok K Meena in New Delhi Monday. The state also sought reconciliation of scheme-related data and release of funds for expenditure incurred between March 2024 and March 2026 during the transition from JJM 1.0 to 2.0. Srinivas held separate meetings with three Union secretaries during his visit to Delhi, raising issues related to drinking water infrastructure, artificial intelligence, cyber security and rural livelihoods. During his meeting with MeitY secretary S Krishnan at Electronics Niketan, discussions focused on strengthening activities under the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Mission in Rajasthan and making the stateâs cybercrime response mechanism more effective. Srinivas briefed the Union secretary on measures being taken and plans to prevent cybercrime and ensure effective action against offenders. He stressed the need to further strengthen the stateâs mechanism to deal with cyber offences. In another meeting with Union rural development secretary Rohit Kansal at Kartavya Bhavan, the chief secretary discussed preparations for the National Saras Mela 2026-27, scheduled to be held in Jaipur from Dec 25, 2026, to Jan 11, 2027. The 18-day fair will be organised by Rajasthan Grameen Aajeevika Vikas Parishad (Rajeevika) at the southern campus of Jawahar Kala Kendra, Shilpgram, and the Indira Gandhi Panchayati Raj and Grameen Vikas Sansthan campus. The Union ministry of rural development has already approved the event. Around 750-800 stalls will showcase and sell products made by women members of self-help groups from Rajasthan and other states. The fair will also feature around 50 food stalls, live handicraft demonstrations, workshops and cultural programmes. Buyer-seller conferences are also planned to help women entrepreneurs establish market linkages. Efforts will also be made to connect self-help group products to digital marketplaces through the Rajasakhi brand. title: Defence, space & nuclear energy: PM Modi, Poland's Tusk bat for deeper ties, doubling trade by 2030
text: PM Modi reaffirms support for peace in Ukraine, West Asia as India and Poland deepen strategic ties NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday reaffirmed India's commitment to supporting peace efforts in Ukraine and West Asia during bilateral talks with his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk, as the two countries agreed to deepen cooperation across strategic sectors amid growing global instability. The leaders held wide-ranging talks at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, exploring avenues for cooperation in defence, space, nuclear energy, critical minerals, green technologies and artificial intelligence (AI). They also discussed regional and global developments and agreed to work towards doubling bilateral trade by 2030. Tusk is on a three-day visit to India amid renewed international efforts to end the war in Ukraine. India, Poland to deepen strategic cooperation Announcing the decisions taken during the talks, PM Modi said India and Poland would expand cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy, while encouraging Polish companies to participate in joint projects. Watch Polish PM Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend' "Today we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space, and nuclear energy. We invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India in all these strategic areas," PM Modi said. "In critical minerals and coal gasification too, we will develop new partnerships with Polish expertise," he added. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the discussions aimed to build on the strategic partnership established between the two countries in 2024 and expand cooperation across several areas. "A new phase in the India-Poland Strategic Partnership. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland held wide-ranging talks today. Building on the Strategic Partnership established in 2024, the leaders explored new avenues of cooperation in areas including AI, green technologies, critical minerals and defence, while further deepening ties in trade, investment, education, culture and people-to-people exchanges. " The two leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to a rules-based international order and reforms of global institutions, including the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). India, Poland aim to double bilateral trade by 2030 PM Modi highlighted the growing economic engagement between the two countries, describing India and Poland as emerging centres of growth, technology and innovation amid global uncertainty. "The world is going through a period of uncertainty and change. Even at this time, both India and Poland are emerging as important centres of growth, technology, and innovation," he said. He said the growing economic strength of both countries had created new opportunities for bilateral cooperation, with the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) expected to further expand trade and investment. "And the India-European Union free trade agreement has further expanded these opportunities. Upon entry into force, this agreement will open up new opportunities for exports of machinery, chemicals, plastics, and engineering goods from India to Poland," he said. "Additionally, we will attract new investments from Poland in sectors such as railways and mobility, advanced manufacturing, food processing, and biotech," he added. PM Modi also expressed confidence that the two countries would work together to develop trusted global supply chains and achieve their shared goal of doubling bilateral trade by 2030. The MEA underlined the importance of the India-EU FTA in strengthening economic engagement. "Both leaders agreed to work together to double bilateral trade by 2030. The leaders underscored the importance of the India-EU FTA, which is set to unlock new opportunities for businesses and industries, giving fresh impetus to economic engagement. The two leaders also exchanged views on regional and global developments, reaffirming their commitment to a rules-based international order and reform of global institutions, including the UN Security Council," it said in a statement on X. PM Modi recalls shared history of India-Poland ties PM Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was rooted not only in diplomatic relations but also in a shared legacy of humanity and compassion. "During World War II, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur sheltered thousands of Polish children and families in India. Poland also extended this spirit of humanity by supporting the safe return of our students from Ukraine in 2022," he added. Jaishankar calls on Polish Prime Minister Earlier on Thursday, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Tusk and discussed ways to deepen cooperation between India and Poland across various sectors. "Pleased to call on Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland. Appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India-Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains," Jaishankar said in a post on X. Tusk on three-day visit to India Tusk arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday evening for a three-day official visit aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in defence, trade and strategic sectors. He was received at the airport by Union Minister of State for Food Processing Industries and Jal Shakti Raj Bhushan Choudhary. Welcoming the Polish leader, the MEA said the visit would provide fresh momentum to bilateral ties. "A warm welcome to Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland on his arrival in New Delhi. He was received at the airport by MoS Raj Bhushan Choudhary. The visit will provide fresh impetus to the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and further deepen our longstanding ties," the MEA posted on X. title: Heirs of Jewish banker have sued Sothebyâs over Â£1.2m painting sale, claiming artwork was looted by Nazis during World War II; a Parisian court to soon give ruling
text: A painting by French Impressionist Camille Pissarro, sold by Sothebyâs for Â£1.2 million in 2024, has become the centre of a legal battle involving the heirs of a Jewish banker whose art collection was seized by the Nazis during World War II. Seven descendants of Salomon Flavian have approached a Paris court seeking to overturn the agreement that allowed the painting to be sold, arguing that most of the family was not consulted before the settlement was reached. The auction house disputes the claim that the artwork was looted and has also challenged the French courtâs jurisdiction. According to The Art Newspaper, which reported on the proceedings in September 2026, the dispute concerns 'Darse de pÃªche et bassin Duquesne, Dieppe, aprÃ¨s-midi ensoleillÃ©e', a 1902 painting depicting the French port town of Dieppe. Sothebyâs sold the work in London on June 25, 2024, for Â£1.2 million, below its estimated price range of Â£1.5 million to Â£2.5 million. The Paris court is expected to deliver its ruling on November 5, 2026. Paintingâs disputed journey through history Pissarroâs painting was owned by Flavian, a Jewish banker and art collector who lived in Paris during the 1930s. His extensive art collection was seized by the Nazis in 1941, and his descendants believe the Dieppe painting was among the works taken. The paintingâs history has attracted scrutiny because it appears in Franceâs postwar RÃ©pertoire des biens spoliÃ©s, a government register of property reported as looted during the German occupation. The register was published between 1947 and 1949 to help identify and recover property that had not yet been returned to its owners. However, the presence of an artwork in the register does not, by itself, conclusively establish every detail of how it changed hands. The paintingâs wartime provenance, or documented history of ownership, is now at the heart of the legal dispute. Sothebyâs catalogue acknowledged Flavianâs ownership and the paintingâs inclusion in the register. It also stated that the work was being offered for sale pursuant to a settlement between its current owner and Flavianâs heirs. The painting subsequently appeared in exhibitions at major art institutions, including Tate in London, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and the Philadelphia Museum of Art, according to reports on the case. Seven heirs challenge settlement The legal challenge is not limited to whether the painting was stolen. It also concerns how the settlement was negotiated and whether all the heirs were properly represented. According to The Art Newspaper, seven family members told the Paris court during a September 18 hearing that only two relatives, Gilles and Nicolas Flavian, had signed the agreement. They argue that the other descendants were not consulted before the deal was finalised. Under the arrangement, the two signatories waived their rights to the painting in connection with the sale. Four months after the auction, other family members reportedly received a letter from Mondex Corporation, a Toronto-based firm specialising in recovering assets lost during the Holocaust. The letter said an 8% share of the net sale price had been accepted on their behalf in exchange for their cooperation. An accompanying account statement referred to a 16% commission associated with the two heirs who signed the agreement. The seven plaintiffs are seeking to have the settlement annulled, arguing that they were excluded from decisions affecting their familyâs claim to the artwork. Sothebyâs maintains that the settlement was disclosed in its catalogue. In a statement reported by The Jewish Chronicle, the auction house said: âThose discussions resulted in a settlement agreement between the consignor and Mondex, which was fully disclosed in our catalogue and pursuant to which the work was sold. â Was the painting actually looted? The paintingâs wartime history remains contested. Sothebyâs and Mondex have relied on provenance research commissioned by the sellers, which concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that the work had been seized by the Nazis. The research, conducted by scholar Mary Kate Cleary, found no reference to the painting in the confiscation lists maintained by the Nazi task force known as the Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg, which was responsible for looting artworks during the war. The research suggested that the painting may instead have been sold by Paris art dealer Paul Rosenberg to British collector Edward Le Bas around 1938, before the Nazi occupation of France. References to Le Bas in historical records were cited in support of this interpretation. The heirsâ lawyer, Corinne Hershkovitch, challenged that conclusion. She argued that the absence of the painting from the Nazi inventories did not necessarily prove that it had not been looted. She also questioned whether the historical records used in the research had been interpreted correctly and argued that additional family archives could help clarify the paintingâs ownership. Mondexâs lawyer, Melina Wolman, maintained that the firm believed the painting had been wrongly registered as looted. Mondex founder James Palmer said the firm had adopted its position after examining the available evidence. The competing accounts mean that the question of whether the painting was forcibly taken from Flavianâs collection remains unresolved. Sothebyâs questions French courtâs authority The auction house has also argued that the Paris court lacks jurisdiction because the transaction took place in London between parties it says had no direct relationship with France. The heirsâ case, however, is rooted in the paintingâs alleged seizure in Paris during the Nazi occupation and the subsequent dispute over the rights of Flavianâs descendants. The courtâs decision could therefore determine not only whether the settlement can be challenged, but also how the familyâs claims will proceed. The ruling is not necessarily a final determination of the paintingâs wartime history or ownership. The case highlights the difficulties that can arise decades after the Holocaust, when artworks have passed through multiple owners, historical records are incomplete and descendants seek to recover property taken from their families. For the Flavian heirs, the dispute involves both the contested history of a painting and the question of whether they were given a meaningful role in the agreement that enabled its sale. For Sothebyâs and Mondex, the central issues include the evidence supporting the looting allegation, the validity of the settlement and the courtâs authority to hear the case. text: How Sabrina Ionescu turned rejection into an NCAA record and WNBA championship(Getty Images) Ionescuâs success is about a lot more than what she has accomplished for the New York Liberty. Sheâs a WNBA champion and Olympic gold medalist for Team USA at Paris 2024, and has become a leading figure in womenâs basketball, grabbing headlines for her leadership, signature footwear and burgeoning commercial portfolio. Her activities outside the court suggest a larger ambition to leave a lasting impression in sports and business, and Ionescuâs career is a case study in how athletic success can lead to opportunities beyond the court. All from global brand partnerships to investments in womenâs soccer and emerging basketball leagues. How Sabrina Ionescu built her business portfolio beyond WNBA Sabrina Ionescuâs commercial portfolio has grown along with her New York Liberty accomplishments. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2020 WNBA Draft, she has evolved into one of the leagueâs best guards, helping lead New York to its first WNBA title in 2024, and she captured an Olympic gold medal with Team USA at Paris 2024 to cement her place in the sport. Celebrity Net Worth estimates Ionescu to have a net worth of $10 million in September 2026. But this is an estimate and not a confirmed accounting of her finances. She makes money from professional basketball, endorsements and business interests, with off-court earnings making up a large portion of her financial profile. What drives Sabrina Ionescuâs endorsement and brand success Nike stays at the heart of Ionescuâs reputation. She was the first womenâs basketball player to have a unisex signature footwear and apparel collection with the company in 2023. The Sabrina line has continued to grow; Nike announced the Sabrina 4 collection in April 2026 and launched it in July. Her presence in both womenâs and menâs basketball has helped make her a recognizable name in performance footwear. Her broader endorsement portfolio has included partnerships with AT&T, BodyArmor, Fanatics, State Farm, Xbox and others. These partnerships allow her basketball audience to engage with companies and Ionescu to create a public profile outside of her performances on the court; in 2025, Forbes estimated her total earnings at $10.5 million, a sign of the growing weight of commercial opportunities in her overall financial picture. How Sabrina Ionescu balances basketball and business interests Ionescu has also studied investments in sports and technology. She became an investor and commercial advisor to Bay FC, a National Womenâs Soccer League club based in the San Francisco Bay Area, in March 2025. She is involved in contributing to commercial strategy and helping the clubâs athletes develop their own endorsement portfolios. The move is more of an interest in helping the growth of womenâs sports in general than just basketball. Her investments have also included Buzzer Media and Nex, and her work with Kevin Durantâs Boardroom and Thirty Five Ventures has broadened her exposure to sports media and business. Those interests could provide opportunities beyond her playing career, although the value of any individual investments and any future returns have not been publicly established. Outside of business, Ionescu is married to NFL player Hroniss Grasu, whom she married in March 2024. She has remained connected to her family roots, the University of Oregon and the communities that molded her. She also has a public profile through youth-sports initiatives with the SI20 Foundation, which aims to increase opportunities for young people through athletics. title: The backstory: From the 'Promised Land' to October 7 - the origin story of Israel-Palestine conflict
text: Tracing the conflict over the land, from ancient Canaan to the modern-day Israel-Palestine conflict. Three years ago, Israel experienced one of the deadliest days in its modern history. Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups launched a large-scale attack from Gaza, crossing the border and attacking Israel during a music festival. More than 1,200 people were killed and 251 people were taken hostage on October 7, 2023, according to the United Nations. The attack led Israel to launch a massive attack in Gaza that has since reshaped the region but remains unresolved. So, the question is why conflict resolution is so complicated. The reasons include the history of the two much before October 7, starting with a âpromised landâ. In modern political and popular discourse, the Jewish connection to the land is said to be going back 3,000 years. The figure refers to the history of the ancient Israelites and the long-standing Jewish religious connection to the land. It all begins with Abraham, a biblical patriarch, and the Jewish belief of the âPromised Landâ. Abraham and the ' Promised Land ' Abraham is one of the central figures in the Hebrew Bible and is regarded in Jewish tradition as the first of the three patriarchs of the Jewish people, followed by his son Isaac and grandson Jacob. He is also an important figure in Christianity and Islam. According to the Book of Genesis, God tells Abraham to leave his homeland and travel to a land that God will show him. That land is subsequently identified in the biblical account as Canaan, an ancient name for a region encompassing parts of present-day Israel and the Palestinian territories, although biblical descriptions of its boundaries vary. God then promises the land to Abraham's descendants. This becomes the basis of the Jewish concept of the âPromised Landâ. For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever. (Gen. 13:15) The biblical story continues through Abraham's son Isaac and grandson Jacob, who is given the name Israel. Thus, Jacob's descendants became known as the âChildren of Israelâ. However, the biblical Land of Israel and the modern State of Israel are not the same thing. The modern State of Israel was established only in 1948. The biblical story belongs to an ancient religious tradition dating back thousands of years. For centuries, however, the land remained central to Jewish religious memory. Even after Jews were dispersed across different parts of the world, prayers and religious traditions continued to focus on Jerusalem and the Land of Israel. Historical map showing the biblical Land of Canaan and its division among the Twelve Tribes of Israel. (Credit US Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division) Ancient homeland to modern political idea For centuries, the Jewish connection to the Land of Israel remained deeply rooted in religion, history and identity. Even after Jewish communities were dispersed across different parts of the world, Jerusalem and the land remained central to Jewish religious memory and prayer. By the late 19th century, that ancient connection began to take on a modern political form. Zionism emerged in Europe as a movement seeking Jewish national self-determination and a homeland for Jews, amid growing antisemitism and persecution. And the territory at the centre of that movement was Palestine, which encompassed much of the land Jews regarded as their historic homeland. But Palestine was not an empty land waiting for a new population. It was home to a predominantly Arab population, including Muslims and Christians, as well as a longstanding Jewish community. As Jewish immigration increased, particularly from Europe, two national movements increasingly came to see the same territory as their homeland: the Zionist movement seeking a Jewish national home, and Palestinian Arabs seeking political self-determination in the land where they lived. That claim to the same territory would become the central question of the conflict that followed. 1917: Britain promises a Jewish national home The First World War transformed the region. At the time, Palestine was part of the Ottoman Empire. During the war, Britain fought the Ottoman Empire and eventually took control of the territory. In 1917, Britain issued the Balfour Declaration, expressing support for the establishment in Palestine of a ânational home for the Jewish peopleâ. At the same time, the declaration said that nothing should be done to prejudice the civil and religious rights of the existing non-Jewish communities in Palestine. For the Zionist movement, the declaration was a major diplomatic breakthrough. For the Arab population of Palestine, however, the prospect of a Jewish national home in a territory where they were already the majority gave rise to concerns and opposition. Britain subsequently governed Palestine under a League of Nations mandate. Jewish immigration increased, while relations between Jewish and Arab communities became increasingly tense and violent. 1947: The UN proposes two states After the Holocaust and the devastation of European Jewry during World War II, international support for a Jewish state grew. Britain eventually handed the Palestine question to the newly established United Nations. In 1947, the UN proposed partitioning Palestine into two independent states - one Jewish and one Arab. Jerusalem was to be placed under a special international regime because of its importance to Jews, Muslims and Christians. Jewish leaders accepted the partition plan but Arab Palestinian leaders and Arab states rejected it. The dispute soon turned into war. 1948: Israel is born, Palestinians experience the Nakba On May 14, 1948, David Ben-Gurion, the head of the Jewish Agency and leader of the Jewish community in Palestine, declared the establishment of the State of Israel and became its first prime minister. The next day, armies from neighbouring Arab states entered the conflict, beginning the first Arab-Israeli war. Israel not just survived the war but ended up controlling considerably more territory than the Jewish state envisaged under the UN partition plan. The Palestinian Arab state proposed by the UN was never established. For Palestinians, it meant that more than half of the Palestinian Arab population fled or were expelled., becoming refugees. Palestinians refer to this mass displacement and dispossession as the Nakba, or âcatastropheâ. Thus, many Palestinians and their descendants continue to demand the right to return to homes and properties from which they were displaced, while Palestinian national politics increasingly came to centre on self-determination and statehood. 1967: The land question becomes even more complicated Another major turning point came nearly two decades later. During the Six-Day War in 1967, Israel captured the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza, along with other territories. The war brought another major displacement of Palestinians and placed the territories at the centre of the conflict that followed. For Palestinians, the West Bank and Gaza became central to their demand for an independent state, while East Jerusalem became a particularly important part of their national and religious claim. The occupation also meant that about 1.2 million Palestinians came under Israeli military control, as per UN's historical account. Israel's government and different political and religious groups have had varying positions on the status of the West Bank, with parts of Israeli society viewing the territory through the biblical and historical framework of âJudea and Samariaâ, the biblical and historical names for the area now commonly known internationally as the West Bank. Map showing the modern-day West Bank and surrounding areas,(Credit US Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division) Israeli settlements were subsequently established in the occupied territories. The settlement issue became one of the most contentious subjects in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations. The UN continues to refer to the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, as occupied Palestinian territory. This is where the ancient idea of the Promised Land intersects most visibly with the modern conflict. So where does October 7 fit into this history By October 7, 2023, the conflict had already passed through major wars in 1948, 1967 and 1973, as well as two Palestinian uprisings known as the Intifadas. There had also been the Oslo peace process, the split between Hamas and the Palestinian Authority, and repeated rounds of fighting between Israel and Hamas. At the heart of the unresolved conflict were longstanding disputes over territory, Israeli settlements, Jerusalem, Palestinian refugees, borders and the creation of a Palestinian state. Then came the Hamas-led attack on Israel three years ago. Israel subsequently launched its war in Gaza. Three years later, October 7 remains the defining date of the current conflict. However, as explained, the actual conflict started much before. Why does the âPromised Landâ still matter The phrase helps explain why the land itself carries such deep meaning. However, coming back to October 7 and the subsequent conflict, it cannot be explained simply as a religious fight over the land promised to Abraham. The backdrop comes from there but the conflict is the result of several layers of modern history. These include the rise of nationalism, European antisemitism and Jewish immigration, the British Mandate, the Holocaust, the creation of Israel and the displacement of Palestinians. The âPromised Landâ is therefore the beginning of the backstory, not the whole story. Still, to understand why the conflict has proved so difficult to end, one has to understand something that predates both Israel and Palestine as modern political entities. You use AI every day. title: Nod to four GCC proposals worth Rs 1,710cr
text: Lucknow: A day after unveiling an ambitious plan to develop Uttar Pradesh into a Global Capability Centre (GCC) hub, the state govt on Tuesday cleared proposals to issue letters of comfort (LoCs) to four companies planning to invest a combined Rs 1,710 crore in Gautam Budh Nagar. The four proposals include an Rs 879-crore investment by Havells India Ltd and Rs 634 crore by LG Soft India Pvt Ltd, both under Noida Authority. Ameriprise India LLP plans to invest Rs 112.84 crore and MetLife Global Operations Support Centre Pvt Ltd Rs 84 crore at Embassy Oxygen Business Park on private land. The cabinet approved the proposals under Uttar Pradesh GCC Policy 2024. While Ameriprise and MetLife will be eligible for incentives under the policy, incentives for Havells and LG Soft will be considered on a case-by-case basis. GCCs undertake technology development, research, financial services, engineering and other global business operations for multinational companies. âThe proposed investments are expected to strengthen UPâs GCC ecosystem and create opportunities for skilled employment,â principal secretary, IT and electronics, Alok Kumar said. title: An ode to tomatoes, and tomato soup
text: Canned spaghetti also evolved from canned tomato soup. (Image - Agencies) Years ago, when we visited my fatherâs sister in Vadodara, she gave us bottles of homemade pumpkin ketchup, which she told us was âas good as tomato ketchup from the marketâ. It wasnât. I remembered that when I read that an Ahmedabad company was recently busted for manufacturing âtomato sauceâ without tomatoes. It used potatoes combined with starch, flavourings, acetic acid (vinegar) and colouring. Presumably it worked better than my auntâs kaddu ketchup, which never made it beyond reluctant family members, while this tomato trickery seems to have been a thriving operation. Ketchup can be made without tomatoes. Malaysian kecap, from which it may derive its name, is a soy sauce. Early Western recipes were made from mushrooms, walnuts and shellfish. Filipinos love banana ketchup, a product developed by food scientist MarÃ­a Y Oroso during World War II, to make up for a lack of tomatoes. Oroso, who died heroically during the Battle of Manila (1945), helped Filipinos survive the war by developing many nutritious products, including this sauce made by cooking bananas, sugar, vinegar and spices. Mostly, though, ketchup now implies tomatoes and there are good reasons for this. The general taste profile of ketchup is sweet-savoury, livened by a tangy kick â this is why sugar and vinegar are in most recipes. They are also high in umami, the savoury fifth taste, which is found in ingredients like mushrooms and shellfish. Really good tomatoes are naturally sweet-savoury, hence the confusion about them being vegetables or fruit. Cooking tomatoes increases their umami content and they are sour when unripe, so a large batch will have enough to give a natural tangy taste. This acidity also prevents tomato preparations from going bad fast. This is a big reason for their popularity in soups, especially those being served in places like the railways, where there might be a lag between preparation and serving. The Times of India in 1933, in an article by a âMrs Elliottâ, commends vegetable soups like tomato for freeing cooks from the tyranny of meat stocks, which make everything into âa tasteless watery concoction in which float odd bits of unrecognisable things. Bridget White-Kumarâs recently published compilation of colonial Indian recipes, History on a Plate, has a recipe for railway tomato soup where a base of fresh tomatoes is spiced with ginger, garlic, chilli and pepper powder, and ketchup added at the end to intensify the taste. No wonder Indian train travellers took to tomato soup so well. There are many ways to play around with recipes for tomato soup, like roasting the tomatoes or adding vodka (ideal for chilled soup). A particularly good one is Lindsey Barehamâs idea of adding plums to tomatoes, both tangy-fruity ingredients combining to make something exceptional. Tomato soup is also important as an ingredient in its own right. Famously, chicken tikka masala is said to have been invented when a British-Pakistani chef, Ali Ahmed Aslam, who ran the restaurant Shish Mahal in Glasgow, got a customer who demanded âgravyâ with his chicken tikka. Aslam opened a can of tomato soup and heated it with cream and spices and poured it on the chicken. Others have claimed this story is a fabrication, but it is one which created its own reality, since many people started making chicken tikka masala with tomato soup. Canned spaghetti is another product that evolved from canned tomato soup. Shane Warne depended on it during his cricketing tours of India, refusing to eat spicy local food. But perhaps the strangest recipe made with canned tomato soup is a cake. The title recipe in Sylvia Plathâs Tomato Soup Cake, a collection of favourite recipes from a range of writers, is one which weâre told the poet cooked the day she wrote her poem Death & Co, just three months before killing herself. The cake is, apparently, excellent, with the fruity acidity of tomato soup balancing the sweetness of the other ingredients. Disclaimer : Views expressed above are the author's own.

title: Travis Scott's Cactus Jack Foundation partners with a fashion scholarship fund to award students $10,000 each and offer hands-on design training to build practical skills
text: Image: Cactus Jack Foundation Travis Scott 's Cactus Jack Foundation has partnered with the Fashion Scholarship Fund (FSF) to support aspiring fashion designers through scholarships, mentorship and practical design training. The collaboration, known as the Cactus Jack Design Ethos 101 programme, offers selected students $10,000 each and access to an online curriculum developed by the Cactus Jack team and its partners. Participants also get the opportunity to take part in immersive learning experiences at the Cact.us Design Center in Houston, Texas. The initiative aims to introduce emerging creatives to the ideas and processes behind Scott's brand, exploring the intersection of fashion, design and music. The partnership has continued across multiple scholarship cohorts, with three new Cactus Jack Design Ethos scholars announced in March 2026. Travis Scott's foundation expands fashion education opportunities Scott's foundation launched the Cactus Jack Design Ethos 101 programme in partnership with the Fashion Scholarship Fund as part of a broader effort to create educational opportunities for aspiring creatives. The programme combines financial support with learning opportunities designed to help students explore fashion and design beyond conventional classroom instruction. Its online curriculum is developed by the Cactus Jack team and its partners, while selected scholars receive mentorship and opportunities for immersive experiences at the Cact.us Design Center. Scott said the initiative was intended to help aspiring creatives explore fashion, design and music while encouraging them to develop their own ideas. Peter Arnold, executive director of the Fashion Scholarship Fund, said the partnership would provide the organisation's network of alumni, current scholars and applicants with access to creative resources, mentors and career development opportunities. Three students named Cactus Jack scholars in 2026 The Cactus Jack Foundation announced three new scholarship recipients at the Fashion Scholarship Fund's annual gala in New York on March 24, 2026. The recipients were Cameroun Blount of North Carolina A&T State University, Caira Coleman of Spelman College and Jasmine Cox of the Savannah College of Art and Design. Scott introduced the scholars at the event, which celebrated recipients from the Fashion Scholarship Fund and the Virgil Abloh "Post-Modern" Scholarship programme, alongside other figures from the fashion and creative industries. The three students joined an initiative that had already supported scholars from earlier cohorts. According to the Fashion Scholarship Fund's announcement, three students from the Class of 2024 received Cactus Jack Design Ethos scholarships, followed by three recipients from the Class of 2025. Each selected Cactus Jack scholar receives a $10,000 award. Across the three cohorts announced for 2024, 2025 and 2026, the nine identified recipients represent $90,000 in scholarship awards. What students learn through Design Ethos 101 The programme is designed to immerse students in the creative world behind Scott's Cactus Jack brand, with a focus on fashion, design and music. Its online educational component features a curriculum created by the Cactus Jack team and its partners. The initiative also includes mentorship and opportunities for selected scholars to participate in hands-on workshops at the Cact.us Design Center in Houston. The foundation says the programme encourages independent thinking and introduces participants to real-world applications of creative concepts, with industry experts guiding them through topics related to design, fashion and music. The practical component gives students an opportunity to engage with design processes in a professional creative environment. However, the programme's published details do not establish that every participant receives a formal internship or guaranteed employment with the Cactus Jack team. Inside the Cact.us Design Center in Houston The Cact.us Design Center is a youth-focused educational facility established by the Cactus Jack Foundation in partnership with TXRX Labs. It opened on November 3, 2021, in Houston, Texas. According to the foundation, the centre provides access to design education, technical training and mentorship for young people. Its facilities support a range of creative and manufacturing disciplines, including graphic design, fashion design, sneaker design, 3D printing, woodworking, laser cutting and fabrication. The centre also hosts programmes intended to help students develop practical skills and explore potential pathways to further education and careers. For the Design Ethos 101 partnership, the centre provides a physical setting where selected scholars can participate in immersive workshops and engage with the creative processes behind the Cactus Jack brand. The foundation's wider educational work includes the Cact.us Sneaker Lab, a design-focused programme that introduces young people in the Houston area to design-led fabrication and manufacturing. Fashion Scholarship Fund's role in the partnership The Fashion Scholarship Fund is a nonprofit organisation that supports students pursuing careers in fashion and related industries through scholarships, mentorship and career development opportunities. Its programmes connect students with educational resources and industry professionals. The organisation also administers the Virgil Abloh "Post-Modern" Scholarship programme, which supports aspiring creatives pursuing opportunities in fashion. The partnership with Cactus Jack expands the fund's network of educational initiatives by introducing students to the relationship between fashion, music and creative brand development. Peter Arnold, the fund's executive director, said the collaboration would give its community access to additional mentors, career development resources and educational opportunities. The partnership therefore combines the Fashion Scholarship Fund's established student network with the Cactus Jack Foundation's creative resources and design facilities. Cactus Jack Foundation's wider educational initiatives The fashion scholarship programme is part of the foundation's broader work supporting education and skills development. Another initiative is the Waymon Webster HBCU Scholarship, named after Scott's grandfather, who was an alumnus and dean of Prairie View A&M University's graduate school. The programme helps students attending historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) who face financial difficulties that could prevent them from graduating on time. The foundation has also established Cactus Jack Gardens, a community initiative that works with elementary schools in Houston to introduce students to gardening, agricultural economics and nutrition. In addition, its partnership with Space Center Houston supports STEM education for Houston Independent School District students. The programme brings students together with educators and NASA engineers to work on design, coding and fabrication projects. What the scholarship programme offers The Cactus Jack Design Ethos 101 partnership combines financial assistance with access to creative education and practical learning opportunities. Selected scholars receive $10,000 each, mentorship and opportunities to participate in workshops at the Cact.us Design Center. The programme also introduces aspiring designers to the creative thinking behind a brand associated with music and fashion, giving them an opportunity to explore how these industries intersect. title: Stephen Curryâs rise to NBAâs highest-paid player was about more than three-pointers, as his career choices and endorsement strategy helped build a $203.6 million fortune
text: Stephen Curry. Image via: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, running through the 2028-29 season. The final year is a player option, a route to a 20th season with the same franchise. Curry was eligible for up to $136 million, so the new deal sits about $20 million below the ceiling. Even with the discount, Curry still tops the 2026-27 salary list at $62.6 million. The numbers point to a career built on more than his three-pointers. A run of contracts, a shoe-brand split and a new apparel deal explain how Curry got here. How did Stephen Curry become the NBAâs highest-paid player? Stephen Curry (Image via Instagram / @stephencurry30) Stephen Curry sits first on the 2026-27 contract list at $62.6 million, ahead of Nikola Jokic at $59 million and Jayson Tatum at $58.5 million. Three contracts and one shaky ankle explain most of the climb. Golden State drafted Curry seventh in 2009. Ankle trouble followed, and by 2012 the Warriors had to decide how much to trust the ankle. They offered a four-year, $44 million extension. It became one of the better bargains in league history. Curry won back-to-back MVP awards and the first two of four titles while playing under it. The large numbers arrived next. In July 2017, Curry signed a five-year, $201.2 million deal, the first in NBA history above $200 million. The contract also made Curry the leagueâs highest-paid player. In August 2021, a four-year, $215 million extension made Curry the first player with two contracts over $200 million. Yearly pay on that one rose from $48.1 million in 2022-23 to $59.6 million in 2025-26. A one-year, $62.6 million extension signed in August 2024 then covered 2026-27. The September deal works differently. Curry was eligible for $136 million and signed for $116 million. Pay drops to $55.7 million in 2027-28 and $60.2 million in 2028-29, with the second year a player option. Golden State general manager Mike Dunleavy said there has never been âa better face to a franchise in professional sports history.â The $62.6 million guard gave the team breathing room too. A smaller number cuts the Warriorsâ future payroll commitment, and it fits a long-held plan to finish a career in one uniform. The agreement arrives after a year in which a right knee injury held Curry to 43 games, though he still averaged 26.6 points. How much has Curry earned from contracts and endorsements? Through the 2025-26 season, Curry had collected $470.1 million in NBA salary. Add $62.6 million for 2026-27 and the $116 million extension, and the projected total reaches $648.7 million, provided the final-year option is picked up. Endorsements, investments and other off-court income sit outside that figure. Shoes carry the other big number. Curry began in Nike gear, then signed with Under Armour in 2013. The partnership grew into Curry Brand in 2020, with Curry serving as its president. A 2023 extension was supposed to run past the end of Curryâs playing days. Instead, the relationship ended in November 2025 and Curry Brand went independent. Under Armour kept releasing previously developed Curry products through 2026 while the brand looked at new partners. In June 2026, Curry signed a 10-year agreement with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning worth more than $400 million, an average of more than $40 million a year. The deal covers signature shoes, basketball apparel, lifestyle products, and golf, with plans for Curry Brand stores in China and the United States. Curry can also sign other athletes under the brand. What else is in Curryâs business portfolio? Beyond sneakers, Curry has endorsement ties with Fanatics, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Panini, Rakuten and 2K Sports. The wider business interests sit under a company called Thirty Ink, covering media, branding, investments and philanthropy. Unanimous Media, co-founded with Erick Peyton in 2018, develops film, television, documentary, publishing and podcast projects with a lean toward sports, family and faith. Curry starred in the 2024 Peacock comedy âMr. Throwbackâ and published the photo book âShot Readyâ in 2025. Other ventures include Gentlemanâs Cut bourbon and Underrated, a platform that gives overlooked young athletes basketball and golf programs with competition, development and exposure. Estimates put Curryâs net worth at $350 million. What are Curryâs biggest career accomplishments? Curry is a four-time champion, winning in 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2022, and the 2022 Finals MVP. Curry has two MVP awards, and the 2016 vote is the only unanimous one in league history. In 2015-16, Curry averaged 30.1 points, made 402 three-pointers and led Golden State to an NBA-record 73 wins. The same season produced a 50-40-90 shooting year at more than 30 points a game, something no other player has done. The list keeps going. Curry has 12 All-Star selections, 11 All-NBA nods, and two scoring titles, in 2016 and 2021. Eight seasons ended with Curry leading the league in made threes. In March 2025, Curry became the first player to hit 4,000 career threes. Internationally, Curry owns gold from the 2010 and 2014 FIBA World Cups and the 2024 Paris Olympics, where late threes helped beat France in the final. As for Curryâs NBA career, he is one of the greatest to play the sport, with several stunning records and titles to his name. Many argue that Steph should be in the Greatest of All Time (GOAT) debate alongside Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan and, of course, LeBron James. Certainly, he deserves the place. Recently, the NBAâs official social media handle posted a short video asking league-wide stars for their opinion on one great NBA skill one would steal. Many called it Curryâs shooting, and some wanted his ball-handling as well. Regardless, Curry is a forged player; he developed into one of the greatest in the game. title: From rejected tomatoes to a sustainable business: How one man built a multi-crore empire and turned agricultural waste into plant-based leather for bags, shoes and fashion products
text: A tomato that does not make it to the market is usually treated as waste. It may be too discoloured, too soft or unsuitable for food processing. But what if these rejected tomatoes could be given a second life, not as food, but as a material used to make bags, shoes and fashion accessories? That is the idea behind Pritesh Mistryâs venture, The Bio Company. The entrepreneur developed a way to turn discarded tomato by-products into bio-leather, a plant-based alternative to conventional leather. What began as a college project has since developed into a business supplying material for fashion, accessories and other applications. The idea addresses two problems at once: agricultural waste and the environmental concerns associated with leather production. Instead of allowing useful plant material to go unused, Mistry is working to convert it into something that can be used by designers and manufacturers. His journey is not simply about making something new from tomatoes. It is about looking at a familiar problem from a different angle. Two problems that led to one unusual idea Mistryâs journey began while he was studying biotechnology at Mumbaiâs Thadomal Shahani Engineering College. During his college project, he visited leather tanneries in Kanpur and saw the pollution associated with the tanning process. Around the same time, visits to farms exposed him to the large quantities of agricultural produce that were being discarded. These experiences made him think about whether one innovation could address both problems. In an interview with The Better India, Mistry explained that he wanted to find a way to use tomato waste while reducing the environmental impact of leather production. He spent months experimenting with tomato by-products, testing different formulations and working to develop a material with the texture and strength required for practical use. Tomatoes were not selected randomly. Their skins and seeds contain natural components, including pectin, that can help give the material flexibility and structure. The company uses discarded tomato material along with biopolymers, plant-based binders and natural fibres to create a leather-like sheet. The process was developed into a product called Bioleather. Mistry's work also received recognition at the 2021 PETA Vegan Fashion Awards, where The Bio Company won the Best Innovation in Textile award. How discarded tomatoes become a leather alternative The process begins with collecting tomato by-products from farms and food-processing units. The material is then processed and combined with other plant-based ingredients to create a flexible sheet that can be used in place of conventional leather in selected products. The company says its tomato-based material avoids polyurethane (PU) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC), two plastics commonly used in synthetic leather. It also describes the product as biodegradable and vegan. These claims are part of the company's material specifications, although the environmental performance of any alternative material depends on its complete composition, manufacturing process and end-of-life conditions. This distinction matters because not every product marketed as vegan leather is necessarily plastic-free. Some alternatives use synthetic coatings or plastic-based layers. The Bio Company has positioned its tomato-based material as an option that avoids PU and PVC. The innovation has also moved beyond the laboratory. Bioleather has been explored for products such as handbags, footwear, jackets and automotive interiors. In The Better Indiaâs report, Toronto-based handbag label Satuhati founder Natasha Mangwani described the material as distinctive because of its origin in rejected tomatoes. The brand began designing samples with Bioleather in 2024 and moved to commercial production a few months later. From a student experiment to commercial production Turning a prototype into a material that manufacturers can use is a different challenge from developing it in a college laboratory. The product must have consistent quality, the right texture and enough durability for its intended purpose. The company has also had to work on sourcing enough tomato waste and increasing production without compromising the material. In a September 2024 interview with Fibre2Fashion, Mistry spoke about the challenges of scaling production and maintaining a consistent supply of tomato waste. He also discussed the need to build partnerships and help potential customers understand how the material differs from traditional leather and other alternatives. A report published by Tomato News in February 2025 stated that The Bio Company was producing around 5,000 metres of Bioleather every month at its facility. Mistry said the capacity could be scaled as demand increased while maintaining quality and sustainability standards. The company has also explored other material innovations. Its current website presents tomato-based leather alongside other plant-based and microbial material projects, showing that its work extends beyond a single agricultural by-product. There is no independently verified public figure available in the sources reviewed to establish that the venture has become a multi-crore empire. Its production capacity, product development and industry recognition, however, offer a clearer picture of how the idea has progressed from a student project to commercial activity. Mistryâs story offers a useful lesson in entrepreneurship: sometimes, an opportunity lies in something that others have already decided to throw away. A rejected tomato may not look valuable, but with research, experimentation and the right process, it can become the starting point for an entirely different product. His work also highlights how innovation can change the way industries look at resources. By finding value in agricultural waste, Mistry has shown that sustainable materials need not remain laboratory experiments but can find a place in everyday products. You use AI every day. title: 'Can't compromise data': Malaysia bans civil servants from using Waze, citing links to Israel
text: Malaysia has barred civil servants from using Waze over data security concerns linked to its Israeli origins Malaysia has banned civil servants from using Alphabet-owned navigation app Waze, citing concerns over data security linked to the app's Israeli origins, following a review ordered by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. The prohibition took effect immediately, according to a letter dated Tuesday from chief secretary to the overnment Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to heads of government agencies. Anwar said the government was examining potential security risks associated with Waze, which he said âwas bound to Israeli lawsâ. âWe cannot compromise on the security of people's data and identities,â news agency Reuters quoted Anwar saying in a Facebook post after chairing a meeting of the national cybersecurity committee on Tuesday. The prime minister did not specify the security risks identified but recommended that government employees use TuJu, a domestic mapping application developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, as an alternative. Waze, founded in Israel, provides real-time traffic updates using satellite signals and data crowdsourced from drivers. Google parent Alphabet acquired the app in 2013 for about $1 billion. The decision comes against the backdrop of Malaysia's strong support for the Palestinian cause. The Muslim-majority country does not maintain diplomatic relations with Israel. You use AI every day. title: Big shake-up before IPL 2027! Mumbai Indians confirm exits of three coaches, including Lasith Malinga
text: Lasith Malinga (PTI Photo/Kamal Kishore) Mumbai Indians have announced that Lasith Malinga , Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson will leave their roles in the menâs team coaching staff. The franchise thanked the three coaches for their contributions and wished them well for the future. "Mumbai Indians thank Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson for their contributions," Mumbai Indians wrote in a statement. Watch Mumbai Indiansâ new coach Luke Williams on Harmanpreet Kaur, WPL auction and plans for 2027 The franchise also acknowledged their commitment and the relationships they built with the team over the years. "Their commitment, the relationships they have built and the memories they have helped create will always be part of our journey. "We wish each of them the very best in their future endeavours." Contributions of the three coaches Malinga, one of Mumbai Indiansâ most celebrated players, played a major role in the teamâs bowling attack during four IPL title-winning campaigns. He also helped the franchise win the 2011 Champions League T20. After retiring as a player, he returned to MI as a mentor and coach, continuing his long association with the team. Mhambrey first worked with Mumbai Indians from 2010 to 2017 before returning in 2024. The former India bowling coach helped develop the teamâs bowlers and brought valuable experience and knowledge of the franchiseâs working culture. Hopkinson joined Mumbai Indians before the 2025 season after working with the England menâs team. He used his international experience to help improve the teamâs fielding standards.
