title: Buxa tigress to be brought back from Assam because of proximity to human habitation, capture operation likely from today: Bengal forest minister Manoj Oraon
text: The Buxa tigress Kolkata: The presence of the Buxa tigress near human habitation in Assam days ahead of the Kali Puja festivities has prompted the Bengal forest department to decide that it would bring her back to Buxa Tiger Reserve, state forest minister Manoj Kumar Oraon said on Saturday. The tigressâs migration from north Bengal to Assamâs Raimona National Park has not triggered any human-tiger conflict yet. âAlthough there has been no conflict situation, the tigress is staying close to human habitation. We have, therefore, decided to capture her and bring her back to Buxa. The Bengal forest dept has already informed its Assam counterpart, which has written to the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) for permission. We hope to get the clearance by Saturday night and will begin the capture operation from Sunday,â Oraon said in Assam, with James Basumatary, executive member (EM) for the forest department, Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC), by his side. âDays ahead of Kali Puja, we donât want to take a chance. Villagers here will burst crackers and that might startle the tigress,â Oraon added. The minister, however, did not specify whether the operation would involve luring the tigress into a cage using bait or tranquillising her. The exact capture strategy is yet to be finalised, sources said. Once brought back, the tigress is likely to be kept in the 2.2-hectare enclosure at the 25th Mile area of BTR. The forest department is expected to use this period to assess her adaptation and wait for suitable conditions before considering another release into the wild. The developments are also likely to accelerate preparations for the next phase of Bengalâs tiger augmentation programme â bringing a male tiger from Biharâs Valmiki Tiger Reserve. The department is expected to initiate arrangements for the translocation. The development bears similarities to the case of Odisha tigress Zeenat, which became a national talking point after she travelled across state boundaries following her release in Similipal. Zeenat crossed into Jharkhand and subsequently Bengal, covering nearly 300 km before being captured in Bankura in Dec 2024 and returned to Odisha. After her return, Zeenat was kept in a soft-release enclosure for several months. Forest officials eventually released her into the wild after detecting signs of male tiger movement in the surrounding landscape. title: In New Hampshire, Bob and Ruth Morrell turned more than 25 German storybook dolls into a village in 1954; Story Land now has more than 50 attractions
text: Cinderella's Castle, the centrepiece of Story Land theme park in Glen, New Hampshire. Credits - WikipediaÂ Story Land in Glen, New Hampshire, grew from a collection of handmade storybook dolls into a theme park for young families. Its founders, Bob and Ruth Morrell, opened the park in late 1954 after dollmaker Frau Edith Von Arps suggested building a village around the figures. The Morrells expanded her idea to include storybook characters, rides and play areas. Story Landâs official history recounts how the idea developed. The park opened with a single ride, a fire engine that Bob drove with children as passengers. Over the decades, it added attractions such as Cinderellaâs Pumpkin Coach and Castle in 1957 and continued expanding. Story Land now advertises more than 50 attractions, including rides, shows and play areas. A knock at the door Bob Morrell had been in the 10th Mountain Division of ski soldiers in the Second World War and had been recalled to service during the Korean Conflict. That took the pair to Germany, when an elderly woman named Frau Edith Von Arps showed up at their home. She was travelling from home to house selling dolls she had handcrafted, one for each classic childrenâs fairy tale. The Morrells became friends with Von Arps, who sold them more than 25 dolls before they returned to New Hampshire. She suggested that they build a small village around the dolls. The Morrells expanded the idea beyond a display, planning rides and play spaces where storybook creatures could live and characters could come to life. This was not their first rodeo in business. They owned the Eastern Slope Ice Cream Company in North Conway, the Concord Monitor reported. The park began with around $5,000, the New Hampshire Union Leader reported. They purchased a piece of land in Glen that the previous owner said wouldnât even make a respectable pasture. Early years of risk The park opened in late 1954, a year before Disneyland came up and transformed peopleâs expectations of amusement parks. According to the Conway Daily Sun, it was once called Story Town and had only one ride, a fire engine Bob drove with youngsters as passengers. Then came a few successful seasons, aided by the arrival of Cinderellaâs Pumpkin Coach and Castle in 1957. Then the national economy stalled, and the fledgling park struggled. The local lenders didnât want the mortgage on the home of the three bears, and the family got by working hard and giving money back into the park year after year. That habit paid off in the late 1960s. Bob bought an old German carousel in 1967 that still turns today, a train and a fleet of boats that became the Swan Boats. The Morrells had room to dream bigger, and visitors began to perceive the park as a location they wanted to return to. Roar-O-Saurus's lift hill and first drop, with the coaster's Triceratops-themed train going down the latter. Credits - Wikipedia A park that kept growing The 1970s were a busy decade. New additions included a chapel, a safari ride, a Moroccan bazaar, the first maze, a Dutch village with a shoe ride and a coaster that later became the Polar Coaster. The 1980s brought a pirate ship, a tea cup ride and a trip to the moon. The parkâs latest new ride was a compact wooden coaster with a 40-foot drop, which opened in 2014. Its more recent major addition was Moo Lagoon, a water play area that debuted in 2024. The park continued as a family business through all this. Ruth handled the gift shop, Bob ran around making sure everyone was having fun, and their daughter Nancy played Mistress Mary in her garden as a child. Their son Stoney continued the work until he died in 2006, and the Morrell family ran the park until 2007, the Concord Monitor reported. Story Land continues to combine storybook settings with rides, shows and play areas for young visitors. The parkâs official media information lists more than 50 attractions and describes its history of entertaining generations of families since opening in 1954. You use AI every day. title: âWe positioned Travis to be world famousâ: How Travis Kelce built a business empire beyond the NFL with help from two brothers who saw his potential early
text: Travis Kelce built a business empire beyond the NFL with help from two brothers who saw his potential early (Getty Images) Travis Kelce is no longer just the Kansas City Chiefs tight end known for making big plays. He has moved into fashion, business and entertainment, with ventures such as Tru Kolors and Garage Beer adding to his growing profile. But this off-field career did not come together overnight. Andre and Aaron Eanes saw an opportunity in Kelce years before his NFL fame and built a plan to turn his personality into a brand that could reach far beyond football. Their story with Kelce began at the University of Cincinnati. What started as a college friendship eventually became a business partnership that helped shape the tight end's career outside the NFL. How Andre and Aaron Eanes saw a bigger opportunity in Travis Kelce Andre first met Travis Kelce through D.J. Woods, the tight end's college roommate and Andre's childhood friend. The two became close at Cincinnati, where Andre was building an event management business. He helped Kelce and his teammates get into parties and other events. Their connection went beyond the social scene. Andscape reported on November 20, 2023, that Andre and Travis Kelce also worked together at a call centre during the period when Cincinnati suspended the tight end from football in 2010 after a failed drug test. Andre and his twin brother Aaron had launched A&A Management in 2011. They wanted to help athletes build businesses and careers that could last beyond their playing days. Kelce became their second client as he prepared for the 2013 NFL Draft. Aaron had a different idea of what athlete management could look like. In a New York Times profile published on January 2, 2024, he explained, "Agents are contract advisers. I thought instead about a music model and building a business where there's coordination with all their external providers." The brothers wanted to handle more than contract negotiations. They focused on commercials, public appearances, media opportunities and other ways to grow Kelce's name. Their ambition was to make him as recognisable as Dwayne Johnson. Andre explained the thinking in the same New York Times profile: "We positioned Travis to be world famous. We didn't know how it would happen, or when it would happen, or what would help push that further along. But it's always been the thought in the back of our minds." How Travis Kelce took that vision into fashion, beer and  other business The brothers' strategy gave Kelce a platform beyond the football field. His commercial work and television appearances helped introduce him to people who did not necessarily follow the Chiefs. He hosted Saturday Night Live in March 2023 and continued to expand his media presence through the New Heights podcast with Jason Kelce. Aaron also explained why he wanted brands to see Kelce as more than an athlete. In Andscape's November 20, 2023, report, he said, "We had a strategy of we want to maximize national commercials to parlay his characters and his ability to be talent throughout the season so that when people are seeing him, they're seeing him as talent, not as the football player." That thinking fits the business interests Kelce has developed. He founded Tru Kolors, his sportswear and lifestyle brand, in 2019. On August 27, 2025, the label teamed up with American Eagle for a limited-edition collection. Kelce served as creative director and took part in the design process. He also entered the beer business with Jason. On June 12, 2024, the brothers announced they had become significant investors, owners and operators of Garage Beer, an Ohio-based brand. The deal gave them roles in areas such as marketing, sales, distribution and expansion. title: At nine, Ethan Sanborn was building Kiid Coffee with his father; by 2026, the young founderâs beverage brand had reached more than 400 retailers
text: Ethan and David Sanborn pitch Kiid Coffee on Shark Tank. Image Credit: PR Newswire While most kids his age were still figuring out what they liked, Ethan Sanborn was helping his father build a beverage business. What started as a family endeavour to create a coffee-flavored drink for kids has gradually blossomed into Kiid Coffee, a growing brand that got national exposure from the TV show Shark Tank. By 2026, the company had expanded its retail presence to more than 400 stores, giving the young founder an opportunity to take a childhood idea into the wider consumer market. Ethan Sanborn established Kiid Coffee with his father The Sanborn family had a personal insight that led to the creation of Kiid Coffee. Ethan liked the taste of his father's coffee and sometimes wanted some himself. But a little boy would not do for traditional coffee. So David Sanborn, his father, began to investigate a different sort of beverage. Ethan also broke both his legs separately, according to Food Republic. Later the family learned that nutritional deficiencies were a contributor and began paying more attention to his diet. So David started working on a drink that would have the similar coffee-inspired flavour that Ethan liked, but also other nutrients. The project eventually developed into a business. All Shark Tank Products reports that the company was founded in July 2023 and officially launched in April 2024. Ethan, who was 7 when the concept was developed, played an important part in shaping the product. Rather than creating another sugary drink aimed at children, the father-son team wanted to introduce something that could become part of a morning routine. The result was a powdered beverage that combined decaffeinated coffee with cacao, prebiotic fibre, vitamins and minerals. Image Credit: Food Republic What made the drink different from conventional children's beverages Kiid Coffee was designed to offer more than the flavour of a regular coffee drink. Its original formulation included organic decaffeinated Arabica coffee, raw cacao, prebiotic fibre and a blend of vitamins and minerals. These included calcium, magnesium, iron, zinc and vitamins A, C, D3, E, B6 and B12. The product was also developed with children's dietary preferences in mind. It contained no added sugar and was designed to be dairy-free, soy-free and gluten-free. Its decaffeination process used water rather than chemicals, with the finished drink described as 99.9% caffeine-free. Parents could prepare it by mixing the powdered beverage with milk or water. The product was available in 3 initial flavours: Original Coffee, Caramel and Chocolate. The flavours were intended to make the drink appealing to children while providing nutrients that might otherwise be missing from their diets. Ethanâs younger brother Logan also helped out in the development process by tasting different batches. Their feedback helped the family refine the flavours, with the Chocolate version resembling hot cocoa and Caramel offering a sweeter taste. How did Kiid Coffee secure a deal on Shark Tank The father-son team took their idea to ABC's Shark Tank in March 2025. According to Food Republic, David and 8-year-old Ethan entered the programme seeking $50,000 in exchange for a 5% stake in their business. During the presentation, the pair explained the product and its intended benefits. The Sharks sampled the different flavours before discussing the company's sales, production costs and plans for growth. Food Republic reported that the drink was being sold for $14, while its production cost was approximately $3.50. Since its launch in 2024, the company has sold $75,000 in products, much of it through direct-to-consumer online sales and Amazon. The presentation attracted the attention of several investors. Kevin OâLeary offered $50,000 for 30%, Lori Greiner and Mark Cuban together offered $50,000 for 20%. Daniel Lubetzky, the founder of KIND Snacks, also offered $50,000 for a 20% share. Ethan attempted to negotiate a smaller equity arrangement, asking for 10% in exchange for the investment. However, after discussing the proposals with his father, he accepted Lubetzky's offer. The agreement also included an additional 5% in stock options if David moved from his part-time involvement to working full-time on the company. The deal provided the young business with an investor who had experience building a consumer food brand. It also gave Kiid Coffee greater visibility beyond its existing online customer base. The business expanded beyond its early online customers The television appearance brought Kiid Coffee considerable attention. Food Republic reported that the company received thousands of orders shortly after the episode aired. Its retail expansion followed quickly. By August 2025, Kiid Coffee was available in more than 150 stores, according to Food Republic. A social media update from August 15, 2025, described the business as a $1 million-a-year company. The growth continued into 2026. In a press release published through PR Newswire, Kiid Coffee announced that it had expanded into more than 400 retail locations across the United States. The company had also entered grocery chains such as Raley's in the Northwest and Fresh Thyme Market in the Midwest. The same announcement stated that the business had surpassed $2 million in annualised sales within 10 months and was on track to exceed $2 million in annual revenue. These figures reflected its projected business performance rather than a confirmed annual financial result. The product range had also grown from three flavours to 5. Alongside Original, Caramel and Chocolate, customers could choose S'mores and Minty Mocha. The company also announced plans for a caffeine-free tea range, extending its focus beyond coffee-inspired drinks. Ethan and David have plans beyond the original product Kiid Coffee's development has also involved teaching children about business and food choices. The family has used Ethan's involvement to show how a product can move from an idea to manufacturing, sales and distribution. David brought previous business experience to the venture. According to All Shark Tank Products, he studied polymer and fibre engineering at Georgia Tech and had established his first consumer brand in 2012. He later launched a pet food seasoning business in 2016, which he scaled and sold in 2020. That experience helped him understand product development and online sales before starting Kiid Coffee. title: 50 AI agents sent to build a Minecraft civilisation turns to bureaucracy; four spent 11 minutes appointing someone to fertilise one wheat block
text: Representative Image AI agents tasked with building a Minecraft civilisation became bureaucratic. In an experiment involving 50 agents, four spent 11 minutes deciding who should fertilise a single wheat block. According to the supplied account of research by Y Combinator and Olam Labs, the group had three hours to build a thriving settlement, but its ambitions narrowed after zombies killed many agents during the first night. The researchers described how âfour agents spent 11 minutes appointing a âsole fertilizer operatorâ for a single piece of bone meal on a single wheat block.â The episode illustrated a coordination problem within the group: even a small farming task became an exercise in assigning responsibility. Researchers said the behaviour âfelt similar to patterns seen while working with coding agents.â From building a civilisation to cautious survival The collaborative experiment, called Civ50, placed the agents in Minecraft to observe how they organised themselves around a shared goal. AI agents are software systems that can take actions through tools, rather than simply answer questions. The supplied account identifies the participants as GPT-6.1 Sol agents. Although deaths during the first night carried little penalty, the attack disrupted their plans. Researchers noted that âmany ambitious initial tasks were abandoned.â The colony subsequently focused on surviving cautiously rather than developing into the thriving civilisation envisioned at the start. The prolonged discussion over fertiliser was one example of the bureaucracy that emerged. The researchers used gaming environments to investigate how groups of agents cooperate, handle setbacks and compete. Such experiments could help developers identify coordination problems, although the observed behaviour came from specific game scenarios. Rival teams took different approaches Separate competitive tests compared GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 agents. In Bed Wars, a Minecraft game mode involving attacks on rival bases while defending a teamâs own, each side had 10 agents. âGPT agents came up with much more aggressive and elaborate strategies,â the researchers reported. Claude agents adopted a more defensive approach. A technical problem also exposed differences in how the teams responded to obstacles. âA tool bug stopped block-breaking. GPT diagnosed it and shared workarounds; several Claudes concluded breaking was impossible,â researchers wrote. In a separate Mindustry strategy-game test, GPT agents won six of seven games against Claude agents. Researchers described the GPT teams as operating more like a hive, while Claude teams combined a single leader with a more democratic decision process. These results come from the reported game tests, not a general ranking of the modelsâ capabilities. The researchers have made the swarm setups open source, allowing others to investigate questions such as whether changing the number of agents or combining different models produces different group behaviour. title: 1,200km reach, Western parts: How Russiaâs new Filin missile adds to Ukraineâs air defence woes
text: Kyiv has repeatedly urged Western allies to accelerate deliveries of air defence interceptors Russia has begun using a new cruise missile, the Filin, against Ukraine, adding to Moscowâs growing arsenal of relatively inexpensive long-range weapons designed to stretch Kyivâs air defences. The missile combines a Russian-made jet engine with electronic components linked to American and Chinese manufacturers, according to Ukraineâs military intelligence agency, HUR, as reported by Kyiv Post. The weapon reportedly entered combat use in late summer 2026. Its emergence highlights Russiaâs efforts to develop cheaper strike systems capable of reaching targets deep inside Ukrainian territory, potentially complicating Kyivâs efforts to intercept repeated waves of drones and missiles. On October 22, HUR released an interactive 3D model, technical specifications and a component database on its War&Sanctions portal. According to Militarnyi, the agencyâs findings indicate that the Filin combines standardised electronics and some 3D-printed components with a Russian propulsion system. Its advertised performance, however, has not been independently verified. Watch Beyond Fighter Jets India Builds New Drone And Missile Engines US electronics, Chinese navigation and Russian firepower According to Kyiv Post, HUR identified 35 electronic components associated with US manufacturers and 22 linked to Chinese manufacturers. The agency said the electronics resemble those found in other Russian missiles and drones, with standardised designs across different onboard units and circuit boards that could help simplify production. The missile was developed by Moscow-based NPO Molniya, part of Russiaâs Tactical Missiles Corporation. Its 3.5-metre-long fuselage and three-metre wingspan are made from carbon fibre and fibreglass composites, while some structural parts are manufactured using 3D printing, Militarnyi reported. The Filin uses a Russian-made R500 turbojet engine manufactured by Reynolds LLC. Its onboard equipment is assembled by St Petersburg-based PLAZ LLC, which is also involved in producing electronics for Russiaâs Garpiya attack drones, according to the Long War Journal. For navigation, HUR identified a Chinese-made inertial navigation system and a 16-channel Kometa antenna designed to improve resistance to electronic warfare interference. The missile launches from a ground-based platform using a solid-propellant booster and reportedly carries either a 50-kg or 100-kg warhead. Russian-advertised specifications cited by HUR put its maximum speed at 800 kmph and its range at up to 1,200 km. The missile can reportedly fly at extremely low altitudes or reach heights of six kilometres, according to Kyiv Post. A cheaper weapon as Ukraineâs air defences face pressure The Filin fits into a broader Russian push towards relatively inexpensive, mass-producible long-range weapons that complement more sophisticated systems such as the Kh-101 and Kalibr cruise missiles. The Long War Journal reported that Ukraine-based analyst Rob Lee said in August that Russia planned to procure more than 1,000 Filin missiles before the end of the year. However, the publication noted that the weapon had yet to see widespread use, leaving the status of those reported procurement plans uncertain. The development comes as Ukraine faces sustained aerial attacks. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently said Russia had launched nearly 2,300 strike drones, 48 missiles and around 1,600 guided bombs in a single week, damaging infrastructure and civilian facilities across nine regions. Kyiv has repeatedly urged Western allies to accelerate deliveries of air defence interceptors. At the same time, Zelenskyy has said Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators were expected to hold technical-level talks in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November.

title: In 1971, Stockholm residents climbed 13 elms slated for a subway entrance; mass protests stopped the felling, and the trees survived
text: The mature elms in KungstrÃ¤dgÃ¥rden, Stockholm, in 2021-50 years after the Elm Conflict, when protests prevented the felling of 13 trees planned for a subway entrance and shops. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons KungstrÃ¤dgÃ¥rden is a central garden in Stockholm that has long served as a gathering place. There are cafes under the ancient trees and blocks in and around the park that have already been remodelled a lot as Stockholm developed. In the course of post-war planning, the centre has always been considered a subject of renewal, which included demolition, construction of roads and of new connections between different places of the city. One such connection, implied building a subway and construction of an entrance nearby. That place was occupied by a line of elms and an ancient tea-house. Those people who disapproved of such development did not limit themselves in expressing their opinion in writing letters only. They organized themselves, watched the construction site and when builders came there with saws, some people sat in the branches of the trees. City 67 and the plan to fell 13 elms for a subway entrance According to StockholmskÃ¤llan, Stockholmâs history portal, the idea emerged in May 1967 when a project called City 67 proposed subway entrances and shops in the park. According to the English- language broadcast of Sveriges Radio celebrating the 40th anniversary of the tree-chopping incident, the town council had previously ordered the demolition of numerous old buildings throughout central Stockholm in efforts to fight poverty, rat infestation and infectious disease. The Sveriges Radio broadcast also reported that an architecture student discovered the tree plan while visiting a classmate in the planning department. Alternative Stad activists got three alternative plans along with this one, where there was no need for the felling of trees and which the city government tried to keep secret; all four plans were posted near the tea house. The municipality insisted that these elms were unhealthy. According to a 2021 Tidningen Syre article marking the 50th anniversary of the protest, the municipality relied on a single assessment, while specialists from SkogshÃ¶gskolan independently reviewed the trees and found them healthy. The night of 11 to 12 May 1971 and the protesters in the branches The official date for the felling was 13 May and Sveriges Radio notes that the protesters did not trust it, so the workmen arrived earlier, in the night between 11 and 12 May. In her study âPreservation and Protest: Counterculture and Heritage in 1970s Sweden,â published in Future Anterior , Thordis Arrhenius describes workmen arriving with chainsaws early on 12 May, a time chosen to get around protesters who had been camping at the site for several weeks. Thousands of protesters took part and the protest was largely non-violent. Protesters climbed into the trees and Sveriges Radio reports that there was then no reasonable way to disperse them. Thousands of Stockholmers kept up the protest for a whole week, sleeping in tents and hammocks, according to the subway art guide Stockholm Art Walk. Atlas Obscura explains that the majority of the elms are still standing and one of them bears chainsaw marks from that night. What Daniel HelldÃ¨nâs 2005 thesis found about the political establishment The doctoral thesis Demokratin utmanas: Almstriden och det politiska etablissemanget , written by Daniel HelldÃ©n at Stockholm University and defended in 2005, examines how politicians in central positions in Stockholm and nationally, together with the editorial pages of Stockholm newspapers, understood the conflict. It also questions the reasons for the politicians of the city getting involved in the events and the relation of the social democrats to the radicalization of the late 1960s. A commemoration of the 50th anniversary of Almstriden, the 1971 Elm Conflict in KungstrÃ¤dgÃ¥rden, when demonstrators occupied and climbed the elms to stop their removal. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons In the press release from Stockholm University about the thesis, it is stated that from the perspective of the politicians, the event turned out to be a failure as they had to give way to something that was referred to as parliament of the streets. The press release explains that the partyâs hierarchical structure was out of step with the spirit of the time. According to HelldÃ©n, in his 2011 interview with Sveriges Radio, the study described above led to permanent changes. Arsenalsgatan 10 and the shift in Swedish planning after 1971 Stockholm Art Walk reports that construction was delayed and the entrance eventually received a new address at Arsenalsgatan 10, which left the elms in place. The Library of Congress subject record for the Elm Conflict describes the dispute as one of the first major, concrete, political clashes at the municipal level in Post war, Sweden. In her study mentioned above, Arrhenius argues that the protest marked a turning point, weakening broad support for the modernisation drive begun in the 1930s and for the Social Democratic governmentâs planning approach. Furthermore, she explained that the shift from the modern impacted the preservation culture of Sweden by widening the definition of historic things. According to a 2011 article in The Local, Ame Fredlund, the assistant director of town planning at the City Council, said the main effect was far greater respect for peopleâs points of view. Decades later, the trees faced a different threat. title: BJP chief accuses Oppn of undermining democracy, warns Cong of losing LoP post
text: BJP national president Nitin Nabin at âLoktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hataoâ rally and padyatra in Bhagalpur on Monday Patna: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday launched a scathing attack on the Opposition while participating in the partyâs âLoktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hataoâ rally and padyatra in Bhagalpur, accusing Congress and its functionary Rahul Gandhi of undermining democratic institutions after facing electoral defeats. Addressing a gathering at Lajpat Park, Nabin asked Rahul to learn from his failures before making false allegations. âIn 2014, 2019, and 2024, the people of the country have consistently placed their trust in the BJP. The nation needs development and strong leadership, not negativity,â he said and alleged that opposition parties accepted democracy when they won elections but questioned the electoral process whenever they suffered defeats. âIf you win, democracy wins; but if you lose, democracy is in danger. When you won in Karnataka, everything was fine, but when you lost in Bihar , you started crying foul, claiming that votes were stolen,â he said. He warned Congress that if it failed to mend its ways, it would not be able to secure even the leader of oppositionâs position in Parliament in the future. Nabin accused Rahul Gandhi and RJD national working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav of insulting the democratic mandate of Bihar and misleading people through false allegations. Referring to the opposition netas, he said, âRejected political forces were questioning constitutional institutions after being defeated by voters.â Speaking at the rally, senior JD(U) neta and deputy CM Vijay Kumar Choudhary said the NDA was committed to defending democracy and would not tolerate attempts to create political chaos. BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi accused opposition parties of spreading fear over the National Population Register, asserting that its implementation in Bihar had not triggered any unrest. NDA functionaries and ministers Nitish Mishra, Dilip Kumar Jaiswal, Santosh Kumar Suman and Deepak Prakash, Khagaria MP Rajesh Verma and former Union minister Shahnawaz Hussain were among those present at the rally.
